articles.title: WSL 2026: Confira o ranking do Circuito Mundial de Surfe | Ge
articles.standfirst: Temporada vai até dezembro com a disputa do título em Pipeline
articles.summary: Acompanhe a classificação da WSL 2026 e as mudanças no Circuito Mundial de Surfe, que terá decisão em Pipeline e dez brasileiros na disputa pelo título.
articles.body:
Foi dada a largada para o Circuito Mundial 2026 da WSL. A temporada deste ano apresenta novidades como o fim das baterias de repescagem e a volta da icônica onda de Pipeline como etapa decisiva. Além disso, o título não está mais decidido no formato Finals como nos últimos cinco anos, quando os surfistas disputaram um mata-mata para conhecer o campeão mundial.

Yago Dora mostra o troféu de campeão mundial de surfe de 2025 — Foto: Ed Sloane/World Surf League

O CT (Championship Tour) 2026 começa com a etapa de Bells Beach, na Austrália, e termina em dezembro no Havaí. Os canais sportv e o ge.globo transmitem todas as etapas ao vivo.

Diferentemente dos anos anteriores, o campeão mundial de surfe de 2026 será conhecido no sistema de pontos corridos. Ou seja, quem terminar o ranking em primeiro será o vencedor do CT deste ano.

Dez etapas serão disputadas na temporada regular, antes do corte, com 36 homens e 24 mulheres (mais do que as 18 de 2025) em ação. Na 11ª e 12ª paradas do circuito, na Filipinas e em Abu Dhabi, respectivamente, só os 24 melhores surfistas do ranking masculino e as 16 do feminino poderão competir – além de convidados da organização. Essa será a pós-temporada.

Quando a WSL chegar a Pipeline, porém, todos os surfistas que iniciaram a temporada poderão voltar ao Circuito para competir no Havaí. Eles lutarão pelo título da etapa, mesmo sem chances de levar o troféu do CT – que necessariamente ficará com atletas que passaram do corte e competiram em Abu Dhabi e Peniche.

Filipe Toledo em Saquarema em 2025 — Foto: WSL

O Brasil será representado por 10 surfistas no CT 2026. No masculino, o time brasileiro será formado por Yago Dora, Filipe Toledo, Gabriel Medina, Italo Ferreira, João Chianca, Miguel Pupo, Samuel Pupo, Alejo Muniz e Mateus Herdy. No feminino, Luana Silva será a única brasuca em busca do título.

A etapa brasileira do Circuito Mundial segue em Saquarema-RJ. O evento na Praia de Itaúna será de 19 a 27 de junho, na sexta parada do Tour.

articles.title: Piloto de paramotor morre após queda causada por linha de pipa | G1
articles.standfirst: O instrutor de Adriano Azevedo presenciou o momento da queda e mostrou o estado do equipamento após o acidente, que ocorreu em Itanhaém (SP).
articles.summary: O piloto Adriano Azevedo morreu após queda de 10 metros em Itanhaém provocada por uma linha chilena que atingiu seu paramotor, conforme relatado por seu instrutor.
articles.body:
Adriano Azevedo dos Santos , de 41 anos, morreu após cair de aproximadamente 10 metros de altura enquanto praticava voo de paramotor em Itanhaém , no litoral de São Paulo. De acordo com a família e instrutor de voo, o equipamento perdeu sustentação após ser atingido por uma linha chilena de pipa.

A vítima morava em Cubatão (SP), mas estava na praia do Bopiranga, em Itanhaém, para praticar o esporte, que era seu hobby há dois anos. A viúva, Ivaneide da Silva Vicente, contou que foi informada sobre o acidente pelo instrutor do marido, que acompanhava o voo no domingo (23).

“A pipa pegou no velame [tecido do equipamento], então ela bateu de um lado do velame, correu o velame por inteiro e quase finalizando o velame, ela cortou [...] É uma asa flexível, é um pano, um tecido que inflado ele se torna uma asa, só que quando ele está murcho não [sustenta]”, disse o instrutor de voo Reinaldo Sanches.

Reinaldo presenciou o acidente e gravou um vídeo com o que restou do equipamento ( assista acima ).

Adriano Azevedo morreu aos 41 anos, após sofrer queda de paramotor em Itanhaém. Suspeita é que acidente tenha sido causado por linha de pipa (à dir.) — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

Adriano foi socorrido com vida, mas morreu no dia seguinte. Segundo a Prefeitura de Itanhaém, a equipe do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) constatou trauma com hematoma frontal, fratura da tíbia e escoriações no paciente.

Os profissionais realizaram manobras de reanimação cardiopulmonar e encaminharam o piloto ao Hospital Irmã Dulce, em Praia Grande. De lá, Adriano foi transferido para o Hospital Ana Costa, em Santos, onde teve a morte constatada na segunda-feira (24).

Em nota, a Prefeitura de Itanhaém informou que uma lei municipal proíbe o uso, o fornecimento e a venda de cerol, linha chilena e outros materiais cortantes em pipas e similares.

“Os pais e/ou responsáveis legais respondem civilmente pelos ilícitos praticados por seus filhos menores ou representados legais, nos termos do disposto no art. 932 da Lei federal nº 10.406, de 10 de janeiro de 2002 – Código Civil”, informou a administração municipal.

A Guarda Civil Municipal de Itanhaém destacou que não recebeu nenhuma denúncia de uso de cerol no domingo. O caso foi registrado como morte suspeita no 2º Distrito Policial de Santos, cidade onde a vítima morreu.

O instrutor Reinaldo Sanches ressaltou que as linhas cortantes oferecem graves riscos para os praticantes de esportes de voo. “É um crime fazer o que eles estão fazendo, usar linha cortante para empinar a pipa”, lamentou.

Ele explicou que Adriano fez a formação de piloto sob sua orientação e já estava apto a voar sozinho. No dia do acidente, Reinaldo acompanhava o voo do ex-aluno apenas como amigo. “A gente tinha um vínculo de amizade enorme”, finalizou.

articles.title: Honda sweeps IndyCar's street circuits: 'It's just a lot of hard work'
articles.summary: Honda engines won all six IndyCar street races in 2026, putting the manufacturer in position for the title over Chevrolet with three races left.
articles.body:
With Andretti Global's Kyle Kirkwood winning the Freedom 250 Grand Prix , IndyCar's final street race in 2026, there was one common denominator in all six street races: They were won by a car with a Honda engine.

Honda went 6-of-6 on the street circuits (two Kirkwood wins, three Alex Palou wins and one from Marcus Ericsson) while Chevrolet, IndyCar's other engine manufacturer, didn't win any.

To sweep the streets, Honda never really had to scrape by in any race, as a Honda engine led 542 of the 597 (90.7%) of the laps on streets this year while claiming 15 of the 18 podium spots. The manufacturer has won 19 of the last 21 street races dating back to 2023, when it also swept the streets.

Honda has won 10 of the 15 races, including Felix Rosenqvist's win in the Indianapolis 500 for Meyer Shank Racing. After Chevrolet closed the gap with three straight wins in June and July, Honda has separated itself by winning four in a row.

"I think the fact that we won the 500 and we also turn around and we're doing it currently on street courses, it makes me proud for the team," Honda Racing Corporation USA vice president Kelvin Fu told IndyStar. "And a lot of it is, it's just not us, it's Andretti and it's (Chip Ganassi Racing), right? It's a combination of their ability to develop their car control and the drivers and surviving a 147-lap, bumpy street course."

This season's schedule called for three of the six street courses to be circuits IndyCar had never visited before. Andretti Global captured all three, with Kirkwood winning the Grand Prix of Arlington and Freedom 250 Grand Prix while Ericsson won the Ontario Honda Dealers Indy at Markham . Not only did a Honda engine win all three races, but the pole was won by a Honda in each of those races, which weren't won by the pole-sitter.

"You're always trying to work with the teams on how they're going to deal with these different situations," Fu said of tweaking engines and preparing course simulators for new tracks. "It's just a lot of hard work between what our engineers do here at the factory. (The engineers) pass it to the trackside group, and the trackside group were posted with each team to do the best we can and make the engine perform for the team."

The last two weekends in Markham, Ontario, and Washington, D.C., have been two-day weekends for teams as opposed to the three-day events that street and road course races typically are. While the Freedom 250 Grand Prix was always supposed to be two days of on-track action, IndyCar's postponement of Friday activities in Markham gave teams and engine manufacturers an unexpected obstacle.

At both races, Honda managed to make the necessary alterations for teams to succeed.

"It forces our engineers to be really flexible," Fu said of the short weekends. "Because you've got the two weeks of Indy for the 500 – which is just like hours of running every day, lots of debriefs – you have time to kind of think things through.

"And then suddenly you've got weekends like Markham and D.C. race where it's like two days, you've got to figure it out fast and on the fly. And it forces our engineers to be creative, and they have to really understand what the engine does, what the teams need and be really in tune with what the whole team is going to need going forward."

Honda now leads IndyCar's engine manufacturer championship 1,316-1,110. After Chevrolet won three straight engine manufacturer championships from 2022 to 2024, Honda is in position to win a second in a row thanks to a season that has seen it pull off five podium sweeps while Chevrolet has none.

Following the 2024 season, Fu, HRC USA president David Salters and the entirety of HRC worked to enhance Honda's engine efficiency to reclaim the championship that it won four times in a row before Chevrolet's three-peat.

"We had to look internally and understand what we need to do to up our game," Fu said. "And I'm immensely proud of what the whole team did at HRC to get both engine performance, but also engine reliability."

Honda will look to close out the championship with three races to go, while Palou and Kirkwood are the two leaders for the driver championship. Honda is the frontrunner for the engine manufacturer championship thanks to its domination on the streets in 2026.

articles.title: NASCAR Top 10 driver rankings updated with a new kid in class ahead of Daytona race
articles.summary: Denny Hamlin remains in the top spot, but look who showed up at No. 10 for the first time ever.
articles.body:
NASCAR Cup Series drivers run Dollar Tree 301 race at New Hampshire

One guy spun forward, another spun back, and one guy decided to introduce himself to our little weekly gathering of the top 10 NASCAR drivers.

Nothing has changed up front , in spite of Denny Hamlin being more than two months removed from his most recent win. That's nothin', Kyle Larson is still on our list and he hasn't won since ... since ... who knows? We quit counting months ago.

Looking ahead just a tad, you're unlikely to see any changes after this weekend's race at Daytona — the Coke Zero Sugar But At Least One Big One 400. This is what some of us still call a "plate race," harkening back to when carburetor restrictor plates sucked away horsepower.

And a plate race is no race upon which to judge racing and racers. Everyone is basically running the same reduced speed and hoping for the best.

Check out our Dale Earnhardt book by clicking here

Nothing to lose or gain at Daytona since he's clinched the top Chase spot and those 25 bonus points.

Best of the rest, for now. Can he do a repeat-repeat and win again at Daytona the way he repeated at New Hampshire? Sure he can. Or maybe he'll wreck.

Back on the top-10 train with a decent run last week.

Recent roll slightly interrupted last week, but barring trouble, you'll have to pass him to get to the front Saturday night.

In a battle for fifth in the standings. Not sure he won't start gathering trophies again beginning in September.

Nearly went a lap at damp New Hampshire (New Damp shire?) before spinning, but recovered well and posted a second straight decent finish.

Muddling along and it's weird because you sometimes forget he's still around.

It's been a rough August. He spun more than a DJ last week.

Hey, look who showed up after yet another great run. How's his staying power?

articles.standfirst: La cercanía entre el circuito y la Ciudad Real Madrid, ambas en Valdebebas, da forma a una singular colaboración que permitirá a Madring utilizar determinadas instalaciones del club durante el evento
articles.summary: La cercanía entre el circuito y la Ciudad Real Madrid, ambas en Valdebebas, da forma a una singular colaboración que permitirá a Madring utilizar determinadas instalaciones del club durante el evento
articles.body: El Real madrid es el nuevo patrocinador del circuito de Madring y del Gran Premio de España de F1, que se celebra del 11 al 13 de septiembre, después del acuerdo anunciado este miércoles por la organización de la prueba. Después de cierta polémica sobre el ruido generado por los F3 y los vídeos de los jugadores en el entrenamiento, queda claro que ambas entidades tiene un perfecto entendimiento y que quiere beneficiarse mutuamente de su vecindad. Además ese fin de semana, la fecha del Real Madrid-Rayo Vallecano no está designada aún, pero teniendo en cuenta que la siguiente semana comienza la Champions, es muy probable que el choque liguero se dispute el sábado y que los jugadores como Courtois y el resto de la plantilla podrán asistir a la F1.  "El Real Madrid se suma al GP de España de F1 como local event supporter de la primera edición en Madring, que se celebrará del 11 al 13 de septiembre",, señala el comunicado. "El acuerdo suma al club de fútbol más laureado a uno de los eventos deportivos más prestigiosos, seguidos e influyentes del panorama internacional que se celebrarán en Madrid. Se da además una curiosa casualidad: la Ciudad Real Madrid y la zona norte de Madring son vecinas en Valdebebas. Apenas 200 metros separan la entrada norte del circuito de la puerta principal de la Ciudad Real Madrid, una cercanía que será especialmente visible durante el fin de semana del Gran Premio". "Las instalaciones del club blanco cuentan con una superficie de 120 hectáreas y alberga las instalaciones en las que trabajan todos los equipos deportivos del club, incluido el primer equipo masculino, femenino, cantera y baloncesto, además del estadio Alfredo Di Stéfano. A escasa distancia se encuentra la parcela de Valdebebas por la que discurre el sector norte de Madring y en la que está La Monumental, la curva más característica del nuevo circuito". "Esta proximidad permitirá incorporar determinadas instalaciones del Real Madrid a la operativa del Gran Premio durante el fin de semana de carrera. Madring amplía así su capacidad operativa apoyándose en unas instalaciones situadas junto al propio trazado". "El acuerdo también llevará al Real Madrid al interior del Gran Premio. El club tendrá presencia en diferentes espacios de hospitality de Madring" durante el fin de semana, donde está prevista la participación de leyendas y otras de sus figuras más destacadas", cierra el comunicado oficial. Hay que recordar que desde noviembre de 2025, el Atlético de Madrid es 'local event supporter' del Gran Premio de España. Y así, el Estadio Metropolitano y acogerá el concierto principal del evento y servirá además como centro de apoyo logístico. Será un punto de encuentro para los aficionados, con experiencias exclusivas, zonas VIP y traslados directos al circuito.  Los dos grandes clubes de la capital estarán así junto a un evento global, con más de 80 millones de seguidores por televisión y unos 150 millones de seguidores a través de medios digitales y redes sociales.

articles.title: Radiation link in flight attendant's breast cancer, French court finds
articles.summary: Former Air France stewardess Sophie Lainault has had her cancer recognised as an occupational disease.
articles.body:
A French court has for the first time recognised cosmic radiation as a factor in the breast cancer of a long-serving flight attendant.

Sophie Lainault, a 59 year-old former stewardess on Air France, sought to have her cancer recognised as an occupational disease, brought on by conditions at work.

This has now been confirmed in a landmark court ruling in the southwestern town of Bayonne, which said that cosmic radiation was one of three carcinogenic hazards arising from her profession. The other two were passive smoking and prolonged night work.

Smoking was authorised on Air France flights until 2000.

The decision means that Lainault, who is in remission from her cancer, can take early retirement with any further treatment fully reimbursed by the French health system.

And by establishing breast cancer as an officially-recognised risk for flight crews, the court has also cleared the way for many other similar claims, lawyers say.

"My dearest wish is that the decision encourages other women who up until now have not had the courage to take this step," Lainault said.

As stewardess and later purser on Air France airliners, Lainault clocked up 12,600 flight hours between 1989 and 2019. More than half of these were at night.

Many long-distance high-altitude flights from Paris would have taken her near the North Pole, where exposure to radiation from space – strictly speaking particles from the sun and other stars – is the most intense.

A study this month at the Harvard Medical School in the US found that flight attendants and pilots had the highest level of radiation-related cancer deaths among more than 500 different professions.

In all, about 6.9% of deaths among flight attendants and 6.7% of deaths among pilots were from radiation-related cancers, according to the analysis.

These proportions were higher than for other professions including nuclear technologists, who are routinely exposed to radiation from non-cosmic sources yet placed 12th on the list, the authors said.

It has long been known that air travel at high altitudes exposes people to cosmic radiation, but the dose for most travellers is regarded as statistically insignificant . Exposure at the poles is more intense because elsewhere the earth's magnetic field acts as a shield.

"In France the link between breast cancer and certain hazards has been established for a number of professions, such as nurses … but this is the first time for an air-hostess," said Lainault's lawyer Elisabeth Leroux.

Air France said it had played no part in Lainault's legal case and had not seen the reasoning behind the court's decision.

"The health and security of our staff is an absolute imperative," it said. "Every employee has a medical accompaniment that goes well beyond the regulatory minimum."

articles.summary: El VR46 hace oficial el fichaje del talento de La Ñora. Tras dos años en Gresini, el murciano correrá con la escudería de 'El Doctor' las dos próximas temporadas
articles.body: Siguen los movimientos en el frenético mercado de fichajes. Después de saberse que Luca Marini dejará Honda para enrolarse en las filas del Tech3 KTM con vistas a 2027 (en el que se iniciará la nueva era de las motos de 850cc), el Pertamina Enduro VR46 Racing Team ha hecho oficial el fichaje de Fermín Aldeguer. De esta manera, el talento de La Ñora se mantiene en la estructura de Ducati, pero cambia los colores del Gresini Racing por los del equipo del legendario Valentino Rossi. Curiosamente, este miércoles de anuncios oficiales en la clase reina del Mundial de motociclismo ha tenido a Il Dottore como denominador común. Por un lado, el cambio de aires de su hermano (Marini) y por otro la contratación del talento murciano para su escudería. Aldeguer, que espera volver a la acción en MotorLand Aragón tras superar sus problemas físicos (aunque previamente el doctor Ángel Charte debe considerarle apto para poder competir) ha evidenciado su ilusión por este cambio de domicilio... aunque siga perteneciendo a la familia Ducati. "Estoy muy contento de dar este paso en mi carrera en MotoGP con el Pertamina Enduro VR46 Racing Team. Firmar con el equipo de Valentino es increíble. Siempre ha sido uno de mis ídolos y una referencia para mí. Creo que tenerlo dentro del equipo podrá ayudarme a mejorar como piloto gracias a sus valiosos consejos", ha recalcado el '54'. "El VR46 Racing Team es el Ducati Factory Supported Team, un equipo extremadamente profesional, y estoy muy feliz de competir con ellos. Con el nuevo reglamento de 2027, mi objetivo será adaptarme a los nuevos neumáticos, pero también a la nueva moto. Contar con la Ducati oficial ayudará muchísimo en la evolución durante la temporada. Será un año en el que buscaremos ser constantes, no cometer errores y pasar el mayor tiempo posible sobre la moto para recopilar información. Estoy seguro de que trabajaremos muy bien con todo el equipo y con los ingenieros de Ducati. Podremos hacer un gran trabajo y aspirar a estar de forma constante entre las cinco primeras posiciones", ha apostillado el competidor de 22 años, que en su primera temporada en la clase reina (2025) acabó como rookie del año. El caso es que el '54' dejará atrás Gresini, donde logró su primera victoria en MotoGP en el Gran Premio de Indonesia 2025, y por eso ha querido tener un bonito gesto con un equipo en el que ha lucido mucho. "No puedo terminar sin agradecer a todo el equipo Gresini Racing y a Nadia (Padovani), que me han ayudado a crecer y me han llevado hasta aquí", ha indicado. Dicho sea de paso, el equipo con sede en Faenza contará el año que viene con Joan Mir y Dani Holgado como su nueva dupla para competir en 2027. Ambos sustituirán a Álex Márquez (que se va a KTM) y el mencionado Aldeguer. Por su parte, el VR46 se quedará sin Fabio Di Giannantonio (militará en las filas de KTM) y Franco Morbidelli (quien se ha apropiado del asiento más deseado del WorldSBK: el aruba.it Ducati). Y se reforzarán con Fermín y Nicolò Bulega, tiránico líder del Mundial de Superbike. El italiano aún no ha sido confirmado, pero tiene el puesto asegurado en el equipo de Rossi para dar su salto a MotoGP.

articles.body: Los vecinos de los barrios colindantes al nuevo circuito semiurbano de Fórmula 1 en Madrid, 'Madring', han expresado su profundo malestar tras registrar niveles de ruido cercanos a los 100 decibelios durante las pruebas previas, superando por mucho los 60 dB tolerables. Ante esta situación, la plataforma vecinal Stop F1 instalará sensores homologados durante el Gran Premio, del 11 al 13 de septiembre, con el fin de recopilar pruebas técnicas para la estrategia judicial con la que buscan impugnar la convivencia del circuito con las zonas residenciales. Las molestias denunciadas no se limitan a los tres días de carreras, sino que abarcan el ruido constante —incompatible con el teletrabajo— y las severas restricciones de movilidad que afectan a todo el distrito de Hortaleza. El montaje y desmontaje de la infraestructura ha generado problemas de tráfico desde abril que se prolongarán hasta octubre. Además, existe una gran preocupación por el inicio del curso escolar el 7 de septiembre, ya que afectará de lleno a la adaptación de los niños más pequeños en un entorno alterado por las obras y los cortes. Finalmente, la plataforma muestra un fuerte escepticismo respecto al retorno económico del evento para el comercio local, señalando que la afluencia prevista de 350.000 espectadores consumirá dentro del propio recinto y no impactará en los pequeños negocios de la zona. Asimismo, califican de insuficientes las alternativas de transporte público e insisten en rechazar que se pretenda monetizar las viviendas desplazando a los residentes, concluyendo que el Gran Premio representa el mayor desastre reciente para el barrio.

articles.title: NASCAR TV Ratings Are In for New Hampshire Cup Series Race
articles.summary: The TV ratings are in for NASCAR’s Cup Series race at New Hampshire Motor Speedway, with USA Network averaging 2 million viewers when excluding the rain dela...
articles.body:
NASCAR's return to New Hampshire Motor Speedway delivered an audience of roughly 2 million viewers despite weather interrupting Sunday's Cup Series race.

USA Network averaged 2.0 million viewers for the Dollar General 301 when excluding the rain delay, according to figures reported by Sports Business Journal's Adam Stern.

When the rain delay is included, the entire broadcast averaged 1.793 million viewers.

The numbers provide another encouraging television result for NASCAR as the Cup Series heads from New Hampshire to Daytona International Speedway this weekend.

New Hampshire Draws 2 Million Viewers on USA Network

Sunday's race was interrupted by rain, complicating the television numbers because viewers were left waiting for racing to resume.

Excluding that delay, however, USA Network's race coverage averaged approximately 2 million viewers.

Including the weather interruption brought the overall average down to 1.793 million.

That still put the complete New Hampshire broadcast ahead of the most recent Cup Series race at Richmond Raceway, which averaged 1.516 million viewers.

It also gives some additional context to NASCAR's recent television audiences. The Cup race at Iowa Speedway averaged 1.929 million viewers, meaning New Hampshire's race-only audience topped both of the previous two Cup events.

The comparisons are not perfectly apples-to-apples given the rain delay and resulting difference between the two New Hampshire figures. Still, the 2 million race-only number is a notable result for USA Network.

NASCAR Heads to Daytona After New Hampshire

The ratings arrive as NASCAR turns its attention toward one of the biggest venues on its schedule.

The Cup Series heads to Daytona International Speedway this weekend for the summer race at the 2.5-mile superspeedway.

Daytona brings a dramatically different style of racing from New Hampshire's 1.058-mile oval, with drafting and pack racing creating the potential for significant swings throughout the field.

It also gives NASCAR another opportunity to build on its recent television audiences.

Richmond drew 1.516 million viewers before Iowa increased that number to 1.929 million. New Hampshire then reached the 2 million mark when the rain delay is removed from the calculation.

Now the attention shifts to Daytona and whether one of NASCAR's most recognizable tracks can keep that momentum going.

articles.title: ADUO: FIA confirm Mercedes granted F1 engine upgrades despite complaints from rivals over test findings
articles.summary: The FIA has confirmed findings from the first two periods of performance review; Red Bull were adjudged to have the strongest engine in the first period, giving the other manufacturers upgrades; watch the Italian Grand Prix at Monza live on Sky Sports F1 on September 4-6
articles.body:
Following the introduction of all-new engines for the 2026 season, Formula 1's governing body implemented an Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) system, designed to allow manufacturers to catch up to the performance of the leading power unit during the rules cycle.

It was revealed in June after the first round of performance assessment, which included the first five rounds of the season, that the FIA had adjudged Red Bull to have the strongest engine and had granted upgrades to Mercedes, Ferrari, Audi and Honda.

The FIA never revealed their findings to the media, but teams and drivers confirmed the outcome publicly, while a document revealing the results was also leaked.

The ruling was seen as controversial because the consensus in the paddock was that Mercedes, whose works team had won the first six grands prix of the season, were being given an upgrade, while Red Bull, who had managed just a single podium in that time, would potentially lose more ground to their rivals.

Red Bull driver Max Verstappen spoke out against the findings, while Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff raised further questions over the FIA's processes when he said in July that his team have "the most powerful power unit".

The FIA refrained from publicly confirming the results while a review was carried out, but now, following the second round of assessment, which concluded with the Hungarian Grand Prix ahead of the sport's summer break, the findings from both periods have been announced.

An FIA statement said: "For the first period: Mercedes were determined to be in the two to four per cent window, and will thus be allowed one additional homologation in 2026 and an additional one in 2027, together with corresponding cost cap and dyno testing increases.

"Audi, Ferrari and Honda were determined to be above four per cent, and will thus be allowed two additional homologations in 2026 and two in 2027, together with corresponding cost cap and dyno testing increases."

While this part of the FIA's statement was confirmation of information that had been leaked in June, their findings for the second period provided a further blow for Red Bull.

Had upgrades made by any of the other teams since June been adjudged to have propelled their performance beyond Red Bull's, the Milton Keynes squad could have been granted their own upgrade opportunity.

However, the statement said: "For the second period, no additional homologations were granted to any of the Power Unit Manufacturers."

That means that Red Bull are at the very least seen to be performing within two per cent of the best engine, and may well still be adjudged to have the strongest power unit.

Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli leads his team-mate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton by 59 points at the top of the drivers' standings, while Verstappen is 130 points back from the Italian in sixth.

Mercedes are 87 points clear of Ferrari at the top of the constructors' standings, while third-placed McLaren, who use a Mercedes engine, have found form with reigning world champion Lando Norris winning the last two races.

Mercedes have been free to use their 2026 upgrade since the first-round results were communicated in June, but are not thought to have done so yet. Ferrari, Audi and Honda are thought to have each introduced one of their two upgrades for 2026.

FIA director of single seater Nikolas Tombazis said: "The FIA has undertaken thorough and exhaustive analysis as part of our ADUO review process.

"With the release of the findings of period two, we are confident that, based on the quality of the data, its analysis is incredibly robust, giving us a high level of confidence in our findings.

"We also have to respect the confidentiality and intellectual property of the teams and their Power Unit Manufacturers in disseminating any details from the findings.

"This is the first year of ADUO so naturally there are areas which we may evolve over time, in discussion with all the PU Manufacturers"

The third ADUO review period commenced with the Dutch Grand Prix over the weekend, and runs until the Mexico City Grand Prix on November 1.

Red Bull have again been found to have the most powerful engine in Formula 1 in the latest rankings by governing body the FIA.

The decision, which mirrors the first set of findings three months ago, will come as a disappointment to the team, who had been hoping to be allowed the possibility to upgrade their engine.

The process has been introduced this year as part of the regulations governing the new hybrid engine regulations, with the aim of allowing manufacturers who have a deficit a chance to catch up.

The FIA's mechanism has been agreed with all the power-unit manufacturers but is nonetheless controversial because Mercedes are widely believed to have the best overall engine performance.

However, the FIA's so-called additional development and upgrade opportunities (Aduo) programme measures only the power of the internal combustion engine.

The electrical elements of the power unit - which account for nearly 50% of the total performance - are not included.

The process is repeated every six races and the latest findings were issued on Wednesday after Sunday's Dutch Grand Prix, the 12th race of the season.

Mercedes have won eight of this season's 12 races so far, and Red Bull, who set up a new engine design and manufacturing facility to produce an engine for this year's new rules, none.

Nikolas Tombazis, FIA director of single-seaters, said: "The FIA has undertaken thorough and exhaustive analysis as part of our Aduo review process.

articles.title: NASCAR’s 2027 Schedule Is Mostly Familiar. The 2027 Chase Isn’t
articles.summary: Most of NASCAR’s 2027 schedule was already known. The real news came in the Chase, where Watkins Glen joins the final 10 and changes the championship equatio...
articles.body:
NASCAR finally announced its 2027 national touring series schedules Wednesday, and perhaps the biggest surprise was that there were no real surprises.

That's because most of where NASCAR will race next season was already well known. Wednesday's reveal simply served to fill in a few holes.

Normally, NASCAR's schedule for the following year begins with a press release, quickly followed by a parade of releases from individual tracks celebrating the dates they were awarded.

Instead, those track announcements trickled out over the past few weeks, allowing fans and media outlets to piece together a rough version of the schedule long before NASCAR officially unveiled it.

The final major piece fell into place Tuesday, when NASCAR announced it would return to San Diego to race on the street course around Coronado Island.

Beyond that, we already knew the preseason Clash would return to Daytona ; North Wilkesboro would host the All-Star Race rather than a Cup Series points race; and Homestead-Miami Speedway would once again host the season finale.

Instead of Chicagoland Speedway hosting the July 4 weekend, NASCAR will race at Iowa Speedway for the holiday. Chicagoland, meanwhile, will once again serve the market rather than the Chicago Street Race.

The decision to scatter individual track announcements in the weeks leading up to Wednesday's big reveal rather than roll everything out at once was very intentional, according to NASCAR Cup Series director Brad Moran.

"We did a little different this year," Moran said Wednesday. "We wanted to pick some of our events and give some of our tracks some time. They had the opportunity to promote their event and their week, give the media and basically everyone else a little time to chat about it.

"So it was released that way intentionally. We felt we were in a pretty good place, obviously getting the schedule out here before the end of August. It was really just to help out the media, the tracks, get a little hype rather than just get kind of buried in one big announcement."

• Dover Motor Speedway returns to a Cup Series points-race date Sunday, May 16, following its 2026 turn as host of the NASCAR All-Star Race.

• World Wide Technology Raceway on Aug. 22, the Coke Zero Sugar 400 at Daytona International Speedway on Aug. 28 and the Southern 500 at Darlington Raceway on Sept. 5 will be the final three regular-season races in the Cup Series and O'Reilly Auto Parts Series leading into The Chase. Darlington swaps with Daytona as the final cutoff race to determine the Chase fields.

• Pocono Raceway will again feature all three national series during its June 11-13 race weekend.

• The Chase for the Craftsman Truck Series will begin at New Hampshire Motor Speedway on Saturday, Sept. 25.

• All three national series will be off during Easter weekend, March 27-28, and again for a summer break Aug. 7-8.

The June race at Michigan International Speedway returns to Father's Day weekend for the first time since 2017. It's a spot the track occupied beginning with its first race in 1969.

But the biggest changes come in the final 10 races that will determine NASCAR's season champions.

Instead of opening The Chase, Darlington will be the final regular-season race for the Cup and O'Reilly Auto Parts Series. That is most likely a one-off swap given that the Darlington race traditionally falls on Labor Day weekend.

Richmond Raceway and New Hampshire Motor Speedway will replace World Wide Technology Raceway and Bristol Motor Speedway in the final 10, with those latter races moving to the summer.

The biggest eyebrow-raiser, though, comes with the addition of Watkins Glen International to The Chase.

It marks the first time a true purpose-built road course will be part of NASCAR's final 10 races. According to Moran, that is a direct result of how dramatically drivers have improved when it comes to racing on road and street courses.

"You know, over time, we've certainly been running more and more road courses," Moran said. "Fifteen years ago or so, you'd bring the ringers in and they'd run up front. That really doesn't happen much nowadays … other than we've got SVG, who's just a worldwide star. One of the best drivers in the world."

Moran said the addition of Watkins Glen is a natural extension of that evolution.

"We have road courses in our regular season, so it only seems fitting that we have a good historical road course, a true road course, in The Chase," he said. "It will fit our series well and our drivers. It's that one road course that kind of evens things up because we have some great road-course stars. And if they're in The Chase, that's one they can circle."

So no, NASCAR didn't exactly drop a bombshell Wednesday.

Most of the bombs had already been dropped one track announcement at a time.

The 2027 schedule, then, is less about where NASCAR is going than what happens when it gets there.

The regular season contains plenty of familiar stops, but the championship format has been shuffled enough to create a very different final 10.

With Watkins Glen joining The Chase and Richmond and New Hampshire moving into the championship fight, NASCAR has quietly made the road to the title considerably less comfortable and may have given its drivers one hell of a championship headache.

articles.title: Toto Wolff's claims that Mercedes can't afford to match rivals' 2026 upgrades assessed by Bernie Collins on The F1 Show podcast
articles.summary: On the latest episode of The F1 Show podcast, Sky Sports' Simon Lazenby, Bernie Collins and Harry Benjamin reflect on the Dutch GP; watch the Italian Grand Prix at Monza live on Sky Sports F1 on September 4-6
articles.body:
The Silver Arrows made a dominant start to the season following the introduction of new chassis and power unit regulations, with Kimi Antonelli winning five races in a row to establish a lead at the top of the Drivers' Championship after his team-mate George Russell had won the opening race.

However, Mercedes have won just two of the six ensuing races, with extra performance added from upgrades helping Ferrari and McLaren to also claim two victories apiece in that time.

The convincing nature of reigning world champion Lando Norris' wins for McLaren at the last two rounds - either side of the summer break - in Hungary and the Netherlands suggests momentum may have swung, with that feeling only heightened by Mercedes boss Toto Wolff saying after Sunday's race that his team "haven't got the money" to match their rivals' upgrades.

Speaking on the latest episode of Sky Sports' The F1 Show podcast , former Aston Martin head of strategy Collins reacted to Wolff's comments and the situation that now faces Mercedes.

"Mercedes have front-loaded it and that shows a confidence in their power unit and their overall chassis design," Sky Sports F1 pundit Collins said.

"We had it for so many years at Force India, having a good reliable car for early-season races before people got on top of their reliability is where we scored all our points.

"For many years we got our strong position in the championship just in the first six races by finishing the race in a reasonable position. So, the front-loading it bit, I get."

While Ferrari and McLaren have regularly brought significant upgrades, Mercedes' first major package since May's Canadian Grand Prix isn't expected to arrive until the rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia from October 2-4, before which there are races in Italy, Spain and Azerbaijan.

Antonelli currently holds a 59-point lead at the top of the standings over Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, with an in-form Norris 83 points back in fourth. In the Constructors' Championship, Mercedes are 87 points clear of Ferrari, while McLaren trail by 162 points.

Collins continued: "Where the money lies, who knows? What the team bosses say to us is often not [the truth]. Maybe Wolff is counting the Mercedes upgrade that is coming to Malaysia [within his calculations].

"Mercedes have sort of put their money on the front end. There are pros and cons to that.

"Getting the points on the board early when other people are struggling is the pro, but conversely, then you're not gathering the data and learning about the development for the next six months when other people are.

"They've put their decision-making one way, and it will be interesting to see if they can hold on."

Changing calendar creates further complication

Collins also pointed out that uncertainty over the remainder of the schedule has created additional complications for teams' upgrade plans.

The Bahrain Grand Prix is taking place in Malaysia, having been postponed in April because of conflict in the Middle East.

The Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, which was also meant to take place in April, was cancelled, while it remains to be seen whether Qatar (Nov 27-29) and Abu Dhabi (Dec 4-6) will be able to host the final two rounds of the season, with European venues on standby to potentially replace them.

"An additional difficulty for the teams has been created by the calendar continuing to change with the ongoing situation in the Middle East," Collins said.

"It's hard for teams to decide whether to put more emphasis on high-speed or low-speed corners, for example, because you don't know what the make-up of tracks going forward is.

"That's quite interesting, where they prioritise their upgrades in terms of overall car performance."

articles.title: MotoGP en verano: qué ocurre en el cuerpo de un piloto cuando el asfalto supera los 50 grados
articles.standfirst: Así es cómo se trabaja para evitar que sientan mareo, vértigos, vómitos, fatiga y dolor de cabeza a consecuencia del calor
articles.summary: Así es cómo se trabaja para evitar que sientan mareo, vértigos, vómitos, fatiga y dolor de cabeza a consecuencia del calor
articles.body: Los grandes premios de verano ponen al límite tanto a las motos como a quienes las pilotan. Con temperaturas que pueden superar los 35 grados, mientras el asfalto alcanza más de 50 grados, cada carrera se convierte en una prueba de resistencia en la que el calor pasa de ser un condicionante externo a convertirse en un rival más. Así será este próximo fin de semana en Motorland Aragón, cuando empiece el decimotercer GP de la temporada. Bajo un mono de cuero, casco y protecciones, el organismo trabaja para mantener la temperatura corporal mientras afronta un esfuerzo físico comparable al de otros deportes de alta intensidad. Por eso, en MotoGP el rendimiento no depende únicamente de la preparación técnica o física. La estrategia médica también forma parte de la competición. Desde semanas antes de cada gran premio, el equipo sanitario de MotoGP, junto con los fisioterapeutas de Quirónprevención y Quirónsalud, adapta los protocolos de hidratación, recuperación y prevención de lesiones a las características de cada circuito. Competir durante cerca de tres cuartos de hora dentro de un mono de cuero limita la capacidad del cuerpo para disipar el calor. Mientras el piloto mantiene un nivel máximo de concentración y soporta fuertes aceleraciones y frenadas, su organismo activa todos los mecanismos posibles para regular la temperatura corporal. Eso sí, a mayor temperatura “más difícil es para el organismo regular su fisiología”, explica el Doctor Ángel Charte, Director de MotoGP Medical Team de Quirónsalud. El riesgo más frecuente es la deshidratación, lo que conlleva “mareos, vértigos, vómitos, fatiga, dolor de cabeza y sensación vasovagal”. De hecho, en los grandes premios celebrados en países asiáticos, donde “la humedad y la temperatura del asfalto son muy elevadas, al terminar muchos pilotos entran en un estado semilipotímico”, afirma. El incremento de la temperatura corporal obliga al organismo a enviar una mayor cantidad de sangre hacia la piel para favorecer la disipación del calor. Ese mecanismo reduce el volumen disponible para abastecer a la musculatura y obliga al corazón a trabajar a mayor intensidad. Paralelamente, la pérdida de líquidos y electrolitos a través del sudor incrementa la sensación de fatiga y acelera la aparición del cansancio muscular. Aunque muchas veces la imagen del piloto sujetando la moto durante las frenadas hace pensar que el esfuerzo se concentra en los brazos, la realidad es mucho más compleja. “Durante una carrera de MotoGP la musculatura más demandada es la del tren superior, con especial importancia en toda la región del antebrazo. No obstante, el cuello, la columna lumbar y otras articulaciones también acumulan mucha carga. Con el calor, la demanda y la percepción de fatiga son aún mayores”, explica Carlos Crespo, fisioterapeuta del MotoGP Health Center Quirónprevención. Según el especialista, el aumento de la temperatura corporal central hace que el organismo desvíe “más flujo sanguíneo hacia la superficie como mecanismo de termorregulación”. A ello se suma la deshidratación, que incrementa la frecuencia cardíaca y termina provocando una fatiga muscular superior a la que se produce en condiciones ambientales más favorables. Pero la exigencia va mucho más allá del tren superior. Aunque es cierto que los hombros y los antebrazos soportan una enorme carga durante las frenadas, “todas las partes del cuerpo trabajan. La posición sobre la moto exige una gran flexión de cadera, rodilla y tobillo, mientras la columna permanece completamente acoplada al depósito y las cervicales deben mantenerse extendidas para conservar la visión. Las piernas también soportan un importante esfuerzo en cada apoyo sobre las estriberas y los aductores trabajan continuamente para estabilizar el cuerpo sobre la moto”, añade Crespo. La planificación médica comienza antes de viajar al circuito y se adapta tanto a las condiciones meteorológicas como a las características técnicas del trazado. De ahí que los pilotos ya de por sí “tengan muy presente la hidratación durante todo el fin de semana, debido al gran esfuerzo físico que realizan”, sostiene Ángel Charte. “Tanto individualmente como los equipos, toman medidas para mantener el máximo de rendimiento a pesar de las temperaturas elevadas. También puede variar la alimentación en fines de semana más calurosos, donde prevalece la dieta ligera”, afirma el Director de MotoGP Medical Team de Quirónsalud. La hidratación constituye uno de los pilares de esa preparación. No se trata únicamente de beber agua, sino de mantener un equilibrio adecuado de líquidos y electrolitos que permita conservar el rendimiento físico durante todo el fin de semana. Para los fisioterapeutas, además, la recuperación empieza prácticamente cuando termina la carrera. “Los cuidados de un deportista deben abarcar una visión de 360 grados: alimentación, hidratación y control del sueño son imprescindibles. Desde la fisioterapia utilizamos técnicas como la crioterapia, la presoterapia, los masajes de recuperación y tecnologías como las cámaras hiperbáricas, la luz roja infrarroja o la radiofrecuencia para acelerar la recuperación fisiológica”, explica Crespo. La preparación médica también cambia según el escenario. Silverstone y MotorLand Aragón representan dos ejemplos opuestos de cómo un circuito modifica la carga física y fisiológica de los pilotos. En Silverstone predominan temperaturas más suaves y un trazado de curvas rápidas y enlazadas que mantiene una elevada exigencia cardiovascular. El trabajo continuo del cuello y los hombros aumenta para soportar las fuerzas laterales, mientras que las condiciones meteorológicas -con lluvia en muchas ocasiones- añaden un esfuerzo extra en términos de concentración y fatiga visual. “Silverstone puede parecer menos agresivo físicamente por sus frenadas, pero exige una concentración extrema y un trabajo constante durante toda la vuelta. No existe ningún circuito poco demandante”, resume Crespo. De cara a este fin de semana en MotorLand Aragón se plantea un desafío completamente distinto. El calor extremo incrementa la pérdida de líquidos y eleva el estrés térmico, mientras que sus fuertes desniveles y frenadas concentran una gran carga sobre piernas, espalda y tren superior. “La comparación entre ambos circuitos refleja perfectamente cómo cambia la fatiga según la temperatura. En Aragón el calor incrementa la percepción del esfuerzo y las fuertes frenadas generan una gran demanda física, aunque la larga recta ofrece un breve margen de recuperación antes de volver a exigir al máximo al piloto”, señala el fisioterapeuta. ¿Cambia la planificación en función del Gran Premio? Charte asegura que desde el punto de vista médico el protocolo siempre es el mismo, aunque reconoce que en carreras donde las temperaturas no son elevadas hay menos probabilidad de deshidratación. “Con todo, el piloto suele trabajar siempre con temperaturas altas por el calor que emite la moto y por el mono que lleva puesto”, describe el responsable del MotoGP Medical Team de Quirónsalud. En algunos casos, se les ve con un chaleco refrigerado para mantenerse frescos, algo que también utilizaron los jugadores de fútbol de la Selección Española durante el mundial. El trabajo médico no termina cuando cae la bandera a cuadros. De hecho, una parte importante del rendimiento del fin de semana depende de la capacidad para recuperarse antes de la siguiente sesión. “El calor extremo activa todos los mecanismos de termorregulación y genera una pérdida importante de electrolitos. Por eso la hidratación previa y posterior es imprescindible, especialmente en un deporte en el que los pilotos están expuestos no sólo al calor ambiental, sino también al del asfalto y al generado por el propio equipamiento de protección”, explica Crespo. Aunque técnicamente sería posible hidratarse durante la carrera, la elevada intensidad del esfuerzo y el nivel de concentración requerido hacen que apenas se utilice esa opción. De ahí que toda la estrategia se centre en optimizar la hidratación antes de la salida y acelerar la recuperación nada más finalizar la prueba mediante reposición de líquidos, crioterapia y el resto de los protocolos fisioterapéuticos. En un campeonato donde las diferencias se miden en décimas de segundo, el calor también forma parte de la competición. Gestionarlo correctamente no sólo ayuda a mantener el rendimiento, sino que constituye un elemento esencial para proteger la salud de unos pilotos que, cada verano, llevan su organismo al límite sobre un asfalto que supera los 50 grados.

articles.title: ¿Está estudiando Aston Martin un regreso con Mercedes?
articles.standfirst: Es uno de los rumores en el paddock tras el fin de semana de Zandvoort, donde hubo una reunión significativa
articles.summary: Es uno de los rumores en el paddock tras el fin de semana de Zandvoort, donde hubo una reunión significativa
articles.body: Se habla de una reunión entre Lawrence Stroll y Toto Wolff en el GP de Países Bajos que ha sido interpretada por algunos medios como la el inicio del regreso de Aston Martin a Mercedes... si Honda vuelve a 'pinchar' en el motor de 2027, donde habrá cambios y exigencias nuevas para la parte de la combustión, con mayor flujo de combustible y un equilibrio 52/42 respecto a la energía eléctrica. En la F1 es raro el día que un directivo de cualquier equipo entra en un motorhome rival, para tratar temas de cualquier tipo. No quiere decir que se tratara ese asunto, pero no es descartable que Stroll, escarmentado de lo sucedido este año, estuviera diseñando un plan 'B' y de paso ejerciendo presión sobre la firma japonesa, cuando ya han empezado a desarrollar el motor del próximo curso. Así lo ha informado @JPEIR0 en su cuenta en X. Los plazos de éxito de Honda apuntan a "estar entre los mejores motores a finales de 2027 o principios del 28", según avanzó este verano el ingeniero jefe, Shintaro Orihara. Si por el camino se volvieran a perder como este curso se verá en los tests de invierno de 2027 y allí habría que tomar una decisión. El actual contrato de Aston con Honda llega al menos hasta 2030, lo habitual de cinco años que suele ser el periodo de una generación o reglamento nuevo. También pudiera ser que Stroll esté hablando ya sobre la próxima generación de propulsores, con la cacareada vuelta de los V8 (no se sabe si con turbo o sin él), con gasolina sintética y sin hibridación o con una muy ligera y no invasiva. Es el modelo que pide Fernando Alonso, que ya no llegará a esos coches cuando vaya a cumplir los 50. En cualquier caso, la relación entre Aston Martin y Adrian Newey con Honda ha mejorado mucho desde el inicio de la temporada, donde el enfado del jefe de equipo era evidente en Australia. "Si lo llegamos a saber, no, no hubiéramos firmado con ellos", aseguraba en la rueda de prensa de los directores en Albert Park, tras señalar todo lo que no habían cumplido en el motor de 2026. Pero ahora vuelve a haber complicidad y el convencimiento de que pueden llegar a tener el mejor motor de la F1 (como le sucedió a Red Bull) en unos meses, tras la restructuración que Honda ha realizado de su proyecto de F1 en Sakura y Silverstone. Los rivales también piensan que volverá a ser una referencia de la parrilla a medio plazo. Suena raro este rumor, cuando las aguas vuelven a su cauce se quiera crear un cisma... salvo que Honda no está dispuesta a seguir con esos V8, cuya implantación definitiva podría producirse en el Consejo Mundial de la FIA esta misma temporada. Habrá que esperar acontecimientos.

articles.title: Jack Miller to leave MotoGP world championship after 16 years
articles.summary: Miller will switch to WorldSBK for the 2027 season
articles.body:
Pramac announced on Thursday that Jack Miller will leave the team following the MotoGP season, with the Australian now expected to complete his move to Yamaha's factory WorldSBK team.

At 31, the Australian rider will leave the MotoGP world championship 16 years after making his debut in 2011, having put together a noteworthy record. The latter features four premier-class victories, although his time in MotoGP was also characterized by instability and a lack of consistency in his results.

Alongside those four wins, Miller has so far claimed 23 MotoGP podiums and two pole positions. However, he will perhaps be best remembered for the remarkable leap he made in 2015, when Honda promoted him directly from Moto3 to MotoGP, in one of the most unusual moves of the modern era.

The rider from Townsville spent his first three seasons in the premier class with Honda before joining Pramac in 2018. The nine podiums he secured with Paolo Campinoti's team, which at the time ran two Ducatis, allowed him to knock on the door of the factory squad, which signed him for 2021.

There, despite three victories and 12 podium finishes, Miller ultimately failed to convince Ducati's decision-makers, who opted not to renew his contract. This opened the door for a move to KTM, where he managed just one podium, which was too poor to justify another contract.

Jack Miller, Red Bull KTM Factory Racing

At that point, ahead of the 2025 season, Campinoti re-entered the picture. The Italian had just ended Pramac's agreement with Ducati to join forces with Yamaha, which was keen to bring in riders with experience like Miller's.

However, the M1's lack of competitiveness has now left Miller with no further options in MotoGP; the arrival of another Australian, Senna Agius, next year has also made him expendable on the grid. Pramac's vacant seat is expected to go to Izan Guevara, who will step up from Moto2 to partner Toprak Razgatlioglu .

"Jack joined Yamaha at an important stage of our MotoGP project and immediately became a very valuable contributor. His technical knowledge, feedback and unwavering commitment helped us make progress in several areas," Yamaha director Paolo Pavesio said.

"Beyond his contribution on track, Jack brought tremendous energy to our team. His positive attitude, spirit and ability to build strong relationships in the garage made him a pleasure to work with."

With his MotoGP career coming to an end, everything appears to be in place for Miller to join Yamaha's factory WorldSBK operation. Nicolo Canepa, Yamaha Europe director and head of the manufacturer's Superbike division, travelled to the most recent grand prix at Silverstone to talk Miller into joining the project.

articles.summary: El de Cervera, un reconocido aficionado del deporte de la pala, cuenta su calvario desde que fue intervenido del hombro el pasado mes de mayo
articles.body: Marc Márquez, siete veces campeón del mundo de MotoGP y también campeón en 125cc y Moto2, ha repasado en una reciente entrevista con 'The Paper' algunos aspectos de su futuro, su estado físico y su vida al margen de los circuitos, con el pádel como protagonista, tras ser operado de nuevo del hombro derecho el pasado mes de mayo. El piloto de Ducati es un gran aficionado al deporte de la pala desde hace años. Es habitual verle compartir en redes sociales algunos partidillos junto a su hermano Álex Márquez, una pasión que también le ha llevado a coincidir sobre el césped con rostros conocidos del deporte, como el gaditano Juan Lebrón o el exfutbolista brasileño Marcelo Vieira. Sin embargo, la intervención quirúrgica le ha jugado una mala pasada... y ha tenido que buscarse un truco. "Antes jugaba mucho al pádel, pero ahora ya no lo hago con el brazo derecho. Intenté aprender a jugar con el izquierdo, pero fue imposible", reconoció. El ciclismo, en cambio, sigue teniendo un papel importante dentro de su preparación física. Márquez también recuerda cómo las lesiones en su brazo derecho le han obligado a renunciar al pádel, otra de sus antiguas aficiones: "Me encanta , forma parte de mi entrenamiento físico". De este modo, incluso cuando se aleja de los circuitos, el campeón de Cervera debe mantener ciertas precauciones. Sus aficiones siguen formando parte de su día a día, aunque las secuelas de sus lesiones le obligan a medir mucho más los riesgos.

articles.title: F1: Alpine to keep Franco Colapinto for 2027 season
articles.summary: Franco Colapinto will remain with Alpine for the 2027 season, the Formula 1 team announces.
articles.body:
Alpine have re-signed Franco Colapinto for the 2027 season.

The move comes midway through a campaign in which the 23-year-old Argentine secured a career-best sixth-place finish at the Canadian Grand Prix.

Colapinto will continue alongside Alpine's lead driver, Frenchman Pierre Gasly, next year.

Alpine executive director Flavio Briatore said: "We have seen Franco truly grow into a great driver this year.

"His results in Miami [where he was seventh] and Montreal especially confirmed what I already knew - that Franco belongs in F1 and he belongs at this team. Having consistency is important.

"We are now settled from a driver point of view and, while this is an important piece of the puzzle, the most significant thing we have to get right is designing and building a fast race car, which absolutely remains our number-one priority."

Colapinto said: "I feel very happy and settled here and it's been even better that we have made significant progress this year compared with last."

Alpine finished last in 2025 but are sixth after 12 races this year, with their best result a podium finish for Gasly in Monaco, although that is subject to a challenge from McLaren.

The appeal hearing was held on Tuesday and McLaren were told to expect a verdict within a couple of weeks.

Alpine's increased competitiveness has been caused by two significant decisions made last year.

They effectively abandoned their 2025 car to enable them to focus fully on the design for the new chassis for this year's new engine rules.

And parent company Renault cancelled its F1 engine programme after 2025 and Alpine have switched to customer Mercedes engines this season.

Colapinto did a half-season for Williams in 2024, after they dropped American Logan Sergeant, and was then signed by Alpine as reserve driver for 2025 - with funding from Latin American sponsors influential in the decision.

He took over from Jack Doohan after the Australian was demoted from a race seat after the first six races of last year.

articles.title: Franco Colapinto: Alpine confirm Argentine driver to remain with team for 2027 season alongside Pierre Gasly
articles.summary: There had been uncertainty over whether Franco Colapinto would be kept on by Alpine for another season; the 23-year-old Argentine is 12th in the 2026 Drivers' Championship; watch the Italian Grand Prix at Monza live on Sky Sports F1 on September 4-6
articles.body:
There had been uncertainty over whether the 23-year-old would be kept on for a second full campaign having been drafted in to replace Jack Doohan after just six rounds of the 2025 season.

The announcement confirms Alpine's driver line-up for 2027, with Colapinto's team-mate Pierre Gasly already signed to a long-term deal.

Alpine executive director Flavio Briatore said: "We are very happy to confirm our driver line-up for 2027 with Franco staying as a race driver alongside Pierre.

"For me, having consistency is very important. We are now settled from a driver point of view and I have said many times that, while this is an important piece of the puzzle, the most significant we have to get right is designing and building a fast race car which absolutely remains our No 1 priority.

"We have seen Franco truly grow and mature into a great driver this year. His results in Miami and Montreal especially confirmed what I already knew: Franco belongs in Formula 1 and he belongs at this team.

"I expect both Franco, and Pierre, to continue doing a fantastic job on track and for the entire team to push relentlessly until we are fighting, and winning, at the front end of this sport."

Colapinto failed to score a points across the 18 rounds he drove in for Alpine last year, but has taken advantage of the team's faster 2026 car to claim six top-10 finishes in the first 12 rounds of this season.

His best performances, referenced by Briatore, came in successive races in May as he finished seventh in the Miami Grand Prix before backing up that result with sixth in Canada.

Colapinto said: "I am very pleased to remain with this team in 2027. I feel very happy and very settled here and it's been even better that we have made significant progress this year compared to last.

"We have a lot more milestones to reach and I know the team is working so hard in finding performance and making the car better and better.

"Our long-term goals are obvious - to compete and win - and I am grateful to the team, Flavio and (managing director) Steve (Nielsen), for the trust placed in me to be one of its drivers going into the future. I'm looking forward to seeing how everything plays out and focusing on my job on-track first and foremost."

Colapinto made his F1 debut in 2024 for Williams when he was named as a surprise replacement for Logan Sargeant for the final nine rounds of the season.

While he was initially without a seat for 2025 as Williams' line-up was already confirmed, his performances, along with sponsorship opportunities that came with his popularity in Argentina, convinced Alpine to sign him on what was said at the time to be a "loan" deal from Williams.

He started 2025 as Alpine reserve driver but was soon given Doohan's seat, with the Australian having faced speculation over his future before the season had even begun.

articles.title: Izan Guevara ficha por Yamaha y correrá con Prima Pramac en MotoGP
articles.standfirst: Los japoneses hacen oficial el ascenso del segundo de Moto2
articles.summary: Los japoneses hacen oficial el ascenso del segundo de Moto2
articles.body: Izan Guevara subirá de Moto2 a MotoGP en 2027. Era algo sabido en el 'paddock' de MotoGP, pero Yamaha lo hizo oficial en la antesala del Gran Premio de Aragón. El balear correrá con el equipo Prima Pramac, junto a Toprak Razgatlioglu, toda vez que Jack Miller deja la escuadra y la categoría -apunta a Yamaha en Superbike-. El mallorquín usa el trampolín que supone el BluCru Yamaha, su actual escuadra de la categoría intermedia, ligada a los nipones, pues va segundo en su clase y primero con una Boscoscuro. El de Palma no escondía que logrará su máximo anhelo. "Para mí, esto es un sueño hecho realidad. Llegar a MotoGP siempre ha sido mi objetivo, y sé lo difícil que es llegar a la categoría reina. Han sido necesarios muchos años de duro trabajo y sacrificios por parte de mucha gente a mi alrededor. Quiero agradecer a Yamaha la confianza que han depositado en mí. Esta oportunidad no sólo es el resultado de mi propio esfuerzo, sino también del apoyo que he recibido de mis padres, mi equipo, mi fisioterapeuta y todos los que me han ayudado a crecer tanto como piloto como persona", decía. El campeón de Moto3 de 2022 espera batallar por la corona de la categoría intermedia a Manu González en lo que queda de curso. "Al mismo tiempo, estoy muy tranquilo porque mi atención sigue centrada en Moto2. Estamos luchando por el campeonato, y mi objetivo es cerrar este capítulo de mi carrera de la mejor manera posible", afirmaba. Izan admite que asciende en un momento ideal. "De cara a 2027, me ilusiona el reto. MotoGP entrará en una nueva era, y creo que eso creará oportunidades para los pilotos que den el salto. Mi primer objetivo será aprender, adaptarme lo más rápido posible y trabajar en estrecha colaboración con el equipo. Luego, paso a paso, quiero seguir mejorando y alcanzar el nivel más alto posible", aseveró.

articles.title: F1 driver contracts: How long are Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Lando Norris and other Formula 1 stars signed for?
articles.summary: Find out how long the likes of Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen and Lando Norris are signed up for at their respective Formula 1 teams; watch every race of the 2026 F1 season, live on Sky Sports and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
Lando Norris agreed to an extension shortly before the start of the 2024 F1 season on a "multi-year" extension to his previous deal, which had been set to expire in 2025.

This means reigning world champion Norris is tied to McLaren until at least the end of 2027.

Oscar Piastri signed a new multi-year contract extension ahead of the 2025 F1 season that will keep him at McLaren until the end of 2028.

Officially, Mercedes announced George Russell only for 2026 after speculation throughout last summer.

But, Sky Sports News understands Russell signed a multi-year contract so will be with Mercedes until at least the end of 2027.

Mercedes confirmed Kimi Antonelli will remain for 2026 at the same time as their October announcement regarding Russell's future.

Sky Sports News understands, like Russell, Antonelli signed a long-term deal that will keep him at Mercedes for at least a third campaign in 2027.

Max Verstappen ended speculation about his future by signing a new Red Bull contract in August 2026 that will see him stay with the team until the end of 2030.

Verstappen citied the possibility of V8 engines returning, confidence in Red Bull and racing in other motorsport categories as some of the reasons behind his new deal.

Isack Hadjar will be the seventh driver in the last eight years to try their hand at being Verstappen's team-mate at Red Bull following his impressive rookie campaign at Racing Bulls.

Hadjar's future will be largely dictated around how close he is to Verstappen, regardless of how strong the RB22 is.

Charles Leclerc penned his latest Ferrari deal in June 2026. As with his previous agreement, announced in January 2024, the team did not publicly comment on the length of his contract, simply saying that it secured Leclerc's future at Maranello "for the coming seasons".

That would take Leclerc up to at least the end of 2028, while there may also be options beyond that to extend further too.

Lewis Hamilton's shock announcement in February 2024 to join Ferrari in 2025 was one of the biggest F1 transfer deals in the sport's history.

Ferrari announced the move as a multi-year deal. Hamilton provided more clarity on the precise length of that term when he confirmed at the 2026 Canadian Grand Prix that he also had a contract in place for at least 2027, which would be his third year at the team. Sky Sports F1 understands Hamilton also holds a unilateral option for 2028 too.

Williams announced during the 2026 summer break a one-year contract extension for Alex Albon that will keep him with the team until the end of 2027.

The short-term nature of the deal perhaps reflects concern in Albon's camp over the team's lack of progress, but also a lack of realistic alternatives being available to him.

A day after Albon's extension was announced, Williams revealed that Sainz had agreed a multi-year extension that appears to tie the Spaniard to the team until at least the end of the 2028 season.

The "multi-year" nature of the deal came as a something of a surprise given Sainz had publicly expressed doubts over remaining with Williams given their poor start to the 2026 season.

Liam Lawson will look to establish himself as the lead driver at Racing Bulls against rookie Arvid Lindblad and should he really impress Red Bull, it should not be ruled out about the possibility of him being in contention to return to the main team.

If that's not possible, Lawson may talk to other teams to secure a spot on the 2027 grid, but he must first deliver some strong results.

British teenager Lindblad is the only rookie on the 2026 grid after impressing Red Bull in his three practice outings last year, finishing sixth in first practice in Mexico City.

The 18-year-old just needs to ensure he does not make any big mistakes and if can match, or beat, team-mate Lawson, at the very least he will have a second season at Racing Bulls.

Fernando Alonso agreed a contract extension in April 2024 to remain with Aston Martin until at least the end of the 2026 F1 season.

Alonso is the oldest driver on the grid and will turn 45 later this year, which would make him the first driver to compete in Formula 1 at that age since Graham Hill in 1975.

Aston Martin appear to be on the backfoot, so there will naturally be questions about whether Alonso will retire at the end of this season.

Lance Stroll is the only driver in the field whose contract details are largely unknown, partly because he is the son of team owner Lawrence Stroll, and appears to have a seat for as long as his father remains in that position.

Stroll has been outperformed by Alonso during their three seasons together but Aston Martin formally announced in June 2024 that the Canadian has a deal for "2025 and beyond".

Oliver Bearman's first full F1 campaign in 2025 saw a mixture of high-profile mistakes and lightning speed - with the latter aspect leading to speculation over whether he could replace Hamilton at Ferrari in the future.

Haas are unlikely to be front-runners in F1 any time soon, so at 20 years old, Bearman could be a key name in the driver market this season, should he impress on the track.

Esteban Ocon's stock has fallen slightly over the last two years after a disappointing end to his time at Alpine in 2024 and being outperformed by Bearman at Haas in 2025.

Ocon will aim to get on top of Bearman in the inter-team battle, which could be important given both drivers have not been confirmed for 2027.

Nico Hulkenberg signed a multi-year contract when he joined Sauber, which is now Audi, in 2025 which means he does not necessarily have a seat beyond this season.

Hulkenberg still seems to enjoy F1 and has not shown any signs of retiring despite being a father and 38 years old.

Gabriel Bortoleto perhaps did not hit the heights many expected after winning the F3 and F2 titles in his rookie seasons on his way to F1.

Bortoleto improved as 2025 went on and is still one of the best young talents on the grid, so it will be in Audi's best interests to keep the 21-year-old.

Pierre Gasly announced a new contract last September to stay at Alpine until at least the end of 2028, having joined the team in 2023.

Gasly has established himself as the lead driver at Alpine and a more competitive car this year could see him cause some surprise results when the top teams trip up.

Franco Colapinto replaced Jack Doohan just six rounds into the 2025 season and recovered from a shaky start to his Alpine career to earn a seat for this season.

The Argentine has impressed Alpine enough to retain his seat for a second full campaign in 2027.

Sergio Perez returns to F1 this year with newcomers Cadillac after a season out of the sport and will be with the American outfit for at least two seasons.

Although Perez was only confirmed for 2026, Sky Sports News understands he signed a multi-year deal.

Valtteri Bottas is also understood to have agreed a multi-year contract that will see him be with Cadillac until at least the end of 2027.

Just like Perez, he spent 2025 on the sidelines but will be hoping to add a few more highlights to his F1 career.

articles.title: Colapinto renueva con Alpine... por lo que Alonso no regresará con Briatore
articles.standfirst: La escudería de Enstone anuncia que Franco sigue en 2027 junto a Gasly
articles.summary: La escudería de Enstone anuncia que Franco sigue en 2027 junto a Gasly
articles.body: No era algo de lo que se estuviera hablando ya, pero fue la comidilla del GP de Barcelona, la posibilidad de que Fernando Alonso regresara a una cuarta etapa en Enstone, después de la de Renault en 2002-06, la de 2008-09 y la última de 2021-22. Finalmente Alpine F1 ha anunciado la renovación de Franco Colapinto por una temporada, por lo que seguirá en el proyecto de Gucci que será el próximo patrocinador principal del equipo que dirige Flavio Briatore. "Estoy muy contento de continuar con este equipo en 2027. Me siento muy feliz y completamente asentado aquí, y es aún mejor que este año hayamos logrado un progreso significativo respecto al anterior. Todavía tenemos muchos objetivos por alcanzar y sé que el equipo está trabajando muy duro para encontrar rendimiento y hacer que el coche sea cada vez mejor", afirma Colapinto. "Nuestros objetivos a largo plazo son evidentes: competir y ganar. Estoy agradecido al equipo, a Flavio y a Steve (Nielsen) por la confianza que han depositado en mí para ser uno de sus pilotos de cara al futuro. Estoy deseando ver cómo se desarrolla todo y, ante todo, centrarme en mi trabajo en pista", asegura. Por su parte, Briatore destaca la importancia de dar continuidad y estabilidad a Alpine . Estamos muy contentos de confirmar nuestra alineación de pilotos para 2027, Ahora estamos asentados desde el punto de vista de los pilotos y he dicho muchas veces que, aunque esta es una pieza importante del rompecabezas, lo más importante que debemos conseguir es diseñar y construir un coche de carreras rápido, y esa sigue siendo nuestra prioridad número uno", subraya. "Hemos visto cómo Franco ha crecido y madurado hasta convertirse en un gran piloto este año. Sus resultados en Miami y Montreal, especialmente, confirmaron lo que ya sabía: Franco pertenece a la Fórmula 1 y pertenece a este equipo. Espero que tanto Franco como Pierre sigan haciendo un trabajo fantástico en pista y que todo el equipo continúe trabajando incansablemente hasta que estemos luchando —y ganando— en la parte delantera de este deporte", cerraba. Señalado por algunos como el piloto de menos nivel de la parrilla en el inicio de 2026, lo cierto es que el argentino ha mejorado en cuanto rendimiento y a seguridad en su pilotaje, con el que ha subido varios niveles en las últimas carreras..

articles.title: Jorge Martín: "Firmaría dos segundos detrás de Marc Márquez"
articles.standfirst: El líder pasa la presión al favorito y campeón
articles.summary: El líder pasa la presión al favorito y campeón
articles.body: Jorge Martín llega al Gran Premio de Aragón de MotoGP como líder, con 31 puntos de ventaja, que son 40 respecto a Marc Márquez, el favorito en la pista turolense. El de Aprilia se siente cada vez mejor con su moto, pero ve complicado batir al ilerdense. Sumar el máximo es su reto para afianzarse. “Me siento igual, a ver si me va igual el fin de semana. Lo importante es que me siento preparado, me siento fuerte, entrenando me he encontrado muy cómodo y creo que estoy mejor de lo que estaba en Silverstone”. “Es muy muy complicado, pero, ahora mismo, no es mi lucha ganarle aquí o no. Obviamente, lo voy a intentar, pero, para mí, es importante centrarme en mi trabajo, en seguir mejorando con la Aprilia, reconfirmar que soy competitivo con la Aprilia igual que lo fui en Silverstone y poquito más”. “Es la misma historia de siempre, es salir, mi equipo cada vez me conoce más, sabe más lo que necesito cuando llego a una pista en la que no he rodado con la moto y ya me preparan una base que me funciona mejor. Entonces, yo creo que ya empezar con esa base me irá mejor que otras veces, pero Aragón es una pista que es peculiar y el año pasado rodaron muy rápido, mucho más que la última vez que estuve aquí, así que, seguramente, mentalmente me tenga que adaptar”. “Las sensaciones de delante, que era un poco lo que buscaba, van mucho mejor, la estabilidad está siendo mucho mejor, pero siempre se puede mejorar. Seguiremos intentando dar pasitos en esa dirección, pero está claro que la moto funciona muy bien, es muy constante en todos los circuitos y muy equilibrada, así que es ver aquí qué necesitamos mañana y buscar en esa dirección”. “Bien o mal nunca lo sabremos. Está claro que no está, hay que desearle ánimo y que vuelva lo antes posible. Son cosas que pueden pasar. Yo me lesioné el año pasado entrenando muy grave para venir a competir. Al final, te estás preparando para llegar lo mejor posible”. “Es un muy buen resultado. Hace dos años fue el que hice y lo firmaría, pero en las carreras nunca sabes. Yo voy a intentar sacar el máximo y veremos qué es el domingo”. “Tengo más experiencia, eso es seguro. Está claro que cada vez me siento más cómodo con la Aprilia. Ése año fue un año difícil porque el asfalto estaba recién hecho y no fueron para nada buenas sensaciones. Creo que llego con una mejor moto de lo que llegué en ese 2024”. “No lo sé. Siento que la moto cada vez es mejor, vamos mejorando mucho y siguen trayendo cosas, así que espero no tocar ese techo y a ver hasta dónde llegamos”. “No sé si mañana voy a estar muerto, así que no voy a estar pensando en Valencia, ni mucho menos”.
