articles.title: Ukraine file formal complaint to FIA ethics committee over decision to lift ban on Russian competitions
articles.summary: The Ukrainian Automobile Federation requests an urgent investigation into its Russian counterpart, the RAF.
articles.body:
Ukraine has lodged a formal complaint with the ethics committee of motorsport's governing body the FIA following the decision to lift the ban on Russian competitors in international events.

The Ukrainian Automobile Federation (FAU) has requested an urgent investigation into its Russian counterpart, the RAF.

The ban on individuals from Russia and Belarus competing in international motorsport events had been in place since Russia launched its invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

The move was approved by the FIA world council, to which sources have told BBC Sport it was proposed by FIA president Mohammed ben Sulayem.

The FAU says the Russian Automobile Federation has "opened and continues to operate" offices in regions of Ukraine occupied by Russia - Crimea, the city of Sevastopol and the Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia Oblasts.

These are recognised by the United Nations as sovereign Ukrainian territory.

The FAU says these actions are in breach of both the FIA statutes and its international sporting code, which permit only one automobile club per country.

FAU president Oleksandr Feldman said: "This is a clear breach of the FIA statutes by the Russian Automobile Federation, which, as an FIA member organisation, is bound to comply with them.

"We urge the FIA president to take urgent action to have these offices closed, and for the Russian automobile federation to be sanctioned for its actions."

The Ukrainian club has requested the FIA ethics committee find the RAF in breach of FIA statutes and order it to close the offices with immediate effect.

The statement also points out that the head of the RAF, Boris Rotenberg, is "directly subject to international sanctions imposed by the US, UK, EU, and other allied jurisdictions in response to aggression against Ukraine".

The decision to lift the ban on Russian and Belarusian competitors followed a similar move by the International Olympic Association.

Following changes to the FIA statutes last year, the FIA ethics committee is under the control of Ben Sulayem and his ally the president of the senate, Carmelo Sanz de Barros.

The FIA has been approached for comment.

articles.title: Hollie Doyle: Marquand and Haggas can claim August Stakes success
articles.summary: Our ambassador Hollie Doyle gives her verdict on the action from Windsor, Goodwood and Sandown, providing her take on the August Stakes, Celebration Stakes and Solario Stakes.
articles.body:
The feature race on Sky Sports Racing on Saturday evening is the Listed Weatherbys August Stakes (6.30) which can go to my husband Tom Marquand and trainer William Haggas.

They combine with the reliable Tenability who has winning form at the track and won't mind any rain, as he proved at Ascot last autumn when he chased home Al Qareem in the Cumberland Lodge.

Tenability has been kept fresh since beating popular stable companion Hamish at Goodwood in June and then finishing third in a Group Three in Deauville over further than this trip.

He brings more compelling recent form to the race than the intriguing Silawi , who has been disappointing given what he achieved in winning the Group One International in Canada last October and then chasing home Opera Ballo in the Jebel Hatta in Dubai in January.

The most prestigious race of the day on Saturday is the Group Two Virgin Bet Celebration Mile Stakes (3.10) at Goodwood and I won't be forsaking the likeable Zavateri , who has a great chance to gain his first win of the year.

Eve Johnson Houghton's three-year-old, who is eased in grade, ran respectably behind Bow Echo in the Sussex Stakes at this track and wasn't disgraced in Notable Speech's Group One at York last weekend.

This is a quick turnaround for a colt who has winning Pattern form at this track in the Vintage Stakes but I take him to win an ordinary renewal at the probable expense of Qirat , last year's shock Sussex Stakes winner who will be a danger to all if he gets loose on the front end.

George Scott must have been tempted to pitch Forty Years On into Stakes company so it's interesting he sets out to exploit an appealing mark in the Virgin Bet Every Saturday Money Back Handicap (2.00) at Goodwood.

This progressive filly, who has been raised 8lb to a rating of 96, made it four from five with a winning reappearance in easy ground at Newbury in early June so any further rain on the South Coast will be a positive.

She's up against Andrew Balding's Ghost Mode , who won at the Goodwood Festival despite hanging badly. He's up four-pound for that and looks her biggest threat, though The Fingal Raven has the form in the book to go well at a much bigger price.

William Haggas's Too Darn Hot gelding High Degree looks capable of giving his rivals weight in the Virgin Bet A Good Bet Handicap (2.35) at Goodwood.

Cieren Fallon's mount was galvanised by first-time cheekpieces at Pontefract a couple of weeks ago and remains lightly enough raced to cope with a four-pound rise.

I do think Gary and Josh Moore's Too Soon looks well handicapped despite winning at Epsom back in early summer and he can give young Warren Fentiman a good ride if he's fully wound up for this return from a three-month break.

I love to see Welsh trainer Chris Mason's All Ways Glamorous run well, just as he did in the Shergar Cup, but he may have to settle for a share of the minor money in the Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap (4.55) at Goodwood.

My preference is for David O'Meara's Toca Madera who ran a big race in defeat at York last week before struggling to make an impact in softer ground there four days later.

He is better judged on his staying on fifth in the Stewards' Cup at this track - a performance that suggests he can take the measure of some battle-hardened rivals in the capable hands of Danny Tudhope in this tough finale.

I'm expecting Secret Of Life to keep her unbeaten record intact in the Group Three BetMGM Atalanta Stakes (2.50) at Sandown on Saturday.

Ralph Beckett's daughter of Pinatubo took the Listed Coral Distaff on Eclipse Day and looks ready for this step up in class in receipt of weight from some classy older fillies.

I'm also keen on Calendar Girl who was a Listed winner on her reappearance at Haydock Park three weeks ago. Like Secret Of Life, she's got an entry in the Group One Sun Chariot so Owen Burrows will be hoping for another step forward.

Both of Sonic Angel 's wins have been achieved ion the All-Weather but Simon and Ed Crisford's colt has the credentials to make a successful turf debut in the Group Three BetMGM Solario Stakes (3.30) at Sandown on Saturday.

I liked the way Oisin Murphy's mount drew clear of the 90-rated Siouxperb on debut at Newcastle before following up under a penalty at Kempton Park this month.

Of course, this demands much more but entries in the Group Two Champagne Stakes and the Group One Dewhurst suggest this son of Dark Angel has a bright future. He can take the measure of Godolphin's promising Yarmouth debut winner Rock Montreal .

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft .

articles.title: Galopin Des Champs retired: Owner Audrey Turley salutes 'one of a kind'  Cheltenham Gold Cup hero
articles.summary: The dual Cheltenham Gold Cup hero Galopin Des Champs was officially retired on Thursday morning after a glittering career and his owner Audrey Turley paid tribute to the 'one of a kind' horse.
articles.body:
The Willie Mullins-trained 10-year-old will go down as one of the most popular National Hunt horses of recent times, with his haul of 12 Grade One victories including back-to-back Cheltenham Gold Cup wins in 2023 and 2024 and a hat-trick of Irish Gold Cups between 2023 and 2025.

He was beaten into third place when bidding for a fourth Irish Gold Cup win in February and that proved to be his final career start as he was ruled out of a sixth appearance at the Cheltenham Festival in March after suffering a setback.

In all Galopin Des Champs won 15 of his 26 career outings and Turley, who ran the black gelding together with her husband, Greg, will always cherish memories that will last a lifetime.

Turley told the Press Association: "We've had the best time of our lives, we really have.

"We never thought this would happen to us. We've had the most wonderful time."

When asked if one day stood out above the rest, she said: "Three Irish Gold Cups and the two at Cheltenham, it's hard to pick out one. Every time it was just a wonderful surprise, it was just magnificent.

"I don't know if I could say one day, maybe the first Cheltenham Gold Cup as that was just extraordinary - like something out of a dream, the joy it brought.

"The other day was in Leopardstown when he won the third (Irish) Gold Cup. Everybody was singing, 'ole, ole, ole' and that just made the hair stand up on the back of our necks.

"People love him and we still have people coming up on Instagram and TikTok saying, 'we miss him, we miss him'. He was so well loved and deserved to be loved, he was just wonderful.

"Everybody did take to him and he was an unassuming character really when you think of it, but he just loved it - I think he enjoyed every bit of it himself."

Turley revealed Galopin Des Champs could now embark on a second career in the equestrian sphere, adding: "He's actually gone over to Ruby Walsh's family and his daughter Isabelle is going to see what he does in that arena, so we'll see if something happens out of that.

"They'll retrain him and see what happens. If he likes it he can do it, if he doesn't we'll have another plan and that's the way it is - it's all about him, whatever he wants to do.

"He'll only be 11 next year and he's still looking fantastic."

While Galopin Des Champs will never again carry the Turley's yellow and brown silks, they have several high-class prospects to look forward to including King Rasko Grey, who provided them with another Cheltenham Festival success in last season's Turners Novices' Hurdle.

"King Rasko Grey has just come back in from the summer and is looking fantastic, so we have high hopes for him," Turley added.

"He did so well in Cheltenham obviously and he's looking like a good horse. He has very big boots to fill, but we won't have another Galopin - he's one of a kind, a diamond. We'll enjoy it whatever happens."

articles.title: George Russell: Mercedes confirm grid penalty but where will British driver take new power unit in 2026 F1 season?
articles.summary: George Russell will face a grid drop later this season for a new engine which could damage his championship hopes; Kimi Antonelli will start at the back for the next race in Monza; watch the Italian Grand Prix at Monza live on Sky Sports F1 on September 4-6
articles.body:
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli will start at the back of the field at the next Formula 1 race in Italy next weekend, but Russell will also face the same repercussions at a race later this season.

Despite having the best car for the majority of this year, both Mercedes drivers have suffered from engine unreliability and will need more than the four allotted power units for this season, thus incurring grid penalties.

"We have not finalised where George will take his penalty, but both drivers will be affected," said Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord on the team's Nu Silver Arrows Radio Show .

"George retired in Canada, Kimi retired in Barcelona, and George also stopped at the end of qualifying in Hungary. Had that happened in the race, the impact could have been much greater.

"We must manage the remaining events so that both cars reach the end of the season with the freshest and best-performing hardware possible. It is a constant trade-off between the risk of running high-mileage components and the points cost of taking a grid penalty and recovering through the field."

Antonelli leads Russell and Lewis Hamilton by 59 points in the Drivers' Championship with 11 scheduled events remaining, although there is uncertainty about the final races on the calendar in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Lando Norris, the winner of the last two races, is 83 points behind Antonelli and could make further inroads at the Italian Grand Prix next Sunday.

Mercedes trackside engineering director Andrew Shovlin says the team will continue to assess where Russell takes his grid penalty.

"Every race adds mileage and learning across Mercedes and the customer teams. Components are checked continually, and we assess whether previous containment measures have solved the underlying issues," he said.

"Our confidence in running a power unit to a sixth or seventh event may be higher in a few races than it is today, so the plans are reviewed after every weekend."

Are F1 budget cap rules the reason for Mercedes' lack of development?

Following their double podium at Zandvoort, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff revealed the Silver Arrows do not have the money to respond to the growing threat from McLaren and Ferrari.

Mercedes have lost their early-season pace advantage and have brought the fewest developments of the front-running teams this season.

On the FIA's upgrades declaration sheet, Mercedes have fitted 24 new parts to their car compared to 37 for Red Bull, 38 for McLaren and 40 for Ferrari.

Since 2021, F1 has had financial regulations which limit the teams' budget they can spend each year to ensure costs do not get out of hand.

Lord suggested the budget cap regulations and Mercedes putting more money into the car at the start of this year means they have less resource for in-season development.

"It is the reality every team faces under the cost cap. Formula 1 organisations must balance headcount and salary costs against the money available for hardware," he explained.

"They must consider how much of the current car was produced this year rather than last, how many spare parts to manufacture and how much stock to carry at the factory and with the race team.

"Every team is trying to find the optimum balance. We continue to find performance in the wind tunnel, but the challenge is deciding when to convert that virtual gain into real parts. With a floor, for example, do you manufacture a new one as soon as performance is found, or align the upgrade with the point at which a fresh floor is required simply to complete the season? Finding those efficiencies is the art within the science.

"A team in catch-up mode may make different choices from one that is leading. By the time we race in Mexico, Brazil and Las Vegas [in November], it does not necessarily follow that another team will have introduced more total performance. It may simply have released it in smaller, more frequent steps."

Shovlin also hinted Mercedes could already be looking at next year's car concept, which is another reason behind their development plan.

"If we believed these [2026] championships depended on having an update at Zandvoort, we would probably have found a way to achieve it," he said.

"We are in the enviable position of leading, so it is logical not to throw as many parts at the current car as competitors who are chasing. We must remain competitive this year while also thinking about the next championship.

"Being in front allows a little more long-term thinking. We have made calculated decisions about the most cost-efficient route to the end of the year. After every race, however, we reassess whether we are doing enough, bringing enough and whether anything can be pulled forward."

Antonelli leads George Russell and Lewis Hamilton by 59 points in the Drivers' Championship but his biggest threat may now come from Lando Norris, who is 83 points behind, but has won the last two races.

Given Antonelli is highly unlikely to win at Monza, it provides a big opportunity for his title rivals to make inroads into their championship deficits.

Ferrari will have huge support from their home crowd, the Tifosi, and are also expected to run new engines in Hamilton and Charles Leclerc's cars - but will not suffer grid penalties.

They hope the extra power will get them back to winning ways after disappointment in Hungary and the Netherlands, tracks Ferrari were predicted to be strong at.

Max Verstappen won last year's Italian Grand Prix and Red Bull could be back towards the front this weekend due to their strong engine.

Monza is one of the four current tracks that feature on the original 1950 F1 World Championship calendar - Monaco, Silverstone and Spa-Francorchamps being the others - and is known as the Temple of Speed thanks to its long straights.

The prime overtaking spot is into the Turn 1 chicane but the battle often continues through the Curve Grande and into Turn 4.

After that comes two 90-degree right handers, known as the Lesmos, before another long straight towards the Ascari Chicane, then the final corner, commonly called Parabolica.

articles.title: Bezzecchi sorprende batiendo el récord... y a los Márquez
articles.standfirst: Marc se reservó en el último intento en la Práctica
articles.summary: Marc se reservó en el último intento en la Práctica
articles.body: Marco Bezzecchi lideró la Práctica de MotoGP del Gran Premio de Aragón, en Motorland. El italiano batió el récord y a los dos Márquez. En esta ocasión, Álex acabó delante de Marc, que se permitió no forzar en su último intento. Las condiciones eran muy buenas, pues ya había menos suciedad en pista, bajo un cielo con ligeras nubes, aire fresco y temperatura agradable, con 24 grados en el ambiente y 47 en el asfalto. Johann Zarco y Fermín Aldeguer pudieron salir pues ya tuvieron el apto definitivo tras el primer libre. Son baja Maverick Viñales y Ai Ogura, suplidos por los probadores Pol Espargaró (KTM) y Lorenzo Savadori (Aprilia). En los primeros compases, todos optaron por salir con neumáticos medios delanteros, con la diferencia entre el trasero, oscilando entre medio y blando, para probar su resistencia con vistas a ambas carreras. Al poco de empezar, en su tercera vuelta, Marc ya distanciaba bastante al resto, que se le iría acercando poco a poco. Jorge Martín se debía ir recto por la escapatoria de la curva 12. Pudo evitar la caída y hasta encontró una vía para volver. Martinator llevaba en una de sus dos monturas un nuevo colín; Bezzecchi lo portaban en las dos. Según Paolo Bonora, el director del equipo de Aprilia, trabajan “ocho días a la semana” para mejorar su actual RS-GP26. No han frenado el desarrollo pese a estar ocupados también con la 850cc de 2027. ‘Bez’, pese a los dolores en la rodilla izquierda, hacía tandas muy buenas en ritmo, que evidencian su mejoría física y la de su máquina en el trazado aragonés. A falta de 17 minutos, después de parar a cambiar neumáticos, empezaron a salir con gomas frescas para buscar un buen registro. Aldeguer era el primero en ir a tope... pero se coló en el Sacacorchos invertido. Sin embargo, el del Gresini perseveró y en el giro posterior se permitió bajar en cuatro décimas el crono del ‘93’. Acosta igualmente rebajaba lo hecho por Marc hasta ese momento. Jack Miller se caía en la curva 2. El australiano se iba rápidamente por el vial intentando llegar al box para coger su segunda moto, pues estaba fuera del corte. Bezzecchi subía la apuesta, pero el mayor de los Márquez replicó al instante con un brutal 1:45.493, batiendo el récord del trazado. Su hermano Álex ascendía a su zaga en la tabla, pero a casi tres décimas de su familiar. Todos retornaban del garaje para el intento final con algunos agobiados, como Pecco Bagnaia, que era la última Ducati y estaba fuera de la Q2. El turinés se posicionó tras Martinator, pero dejando bastante espacio con él. Jorge lo vio y cortó para ponerse detrás. Luego, el del Ducati oficial tuvo un susto tras el primer ángulo y perdió una intentona. Marc volvía, pero sin gomas nuevas. El que sí forzó fue Bezzecchi, que, para sorpresa de casi todos, pudo con el de Cervera por 38 milésimas. Impresionante. Los aplausos en Aprilia resonaban por todo Motorland. La amenaza para ‘Bez’ fue Márquez, pero Álex. Al del Gresini le faltaron sólo 10 milésimas para batirle. El récord y el primer lugar fueron para Marc. Bagnaia se volvía a ir largo y no pasaba el corte... para alegría de Zarco, que sí lo hizo en su vuelta. Pecco entró en su box y se fue por la puerta de atrás sin parar a hablar con nadie. Así, el ‘top 10’ y los que van a la Q2 fueron: Bezzecchi, Álex Márquez, Marc Márquez, Di Giannantonio, Aldeguer, Raúl Fernández, Jorge Martín, Acosta, Morbidelli y Zarco. A la Q1: Moreira, Marini, Bagnaia, Quartararo, Mir, Rins, Bastianini, Binder, Miller, Pol Espargaró, Toprak Razgatlioglu y Savadori. En Moto3, la sorpresa fue que Brian Uriarte no logró pasar directo a la Q2, cosa que sí hizo el líder Quiles. Mandó Almansa. El ‘top 14’ fue: Almansa, Salmela, Perrone, Adrián Fernández, Carpe, O’Gorman, Ríos, Quiles, Bertelle, Pini, Morelli, Cruces, Kelso y Danish. A la Q1: Ogden, David González (sustituto de David Muñoz), Brian Uriarte, Moodley, Pratama, O’Shea, Yamanaka, Rammerstorfer, Carraro, Joel Esteban, Mitani y Buchanan. En Moto2, Iván Ortolá batió el récord y sólo Holgado le dio réplica. David Alonso se quedó fuera pese a su crecimiento final. A la Q2 van: Ortolá, Holgado, Agius, Alonso López,Vietti, Manu González, Dani Muñoz, Escrig, Veijer, Izan Guevara, Sasaki, Baltus, Piqueras y Furusato. A la repesca: Salac, Huertas, Aji, David Alonso, Roberts, Lunetta, Rueda, Arbolino, Öncü, Ferrández, García Dols, Canet, Ramírez, Van den Goorbergh y Zurutuza.

articles.title: Toni Bou y el 40º título: en Cahors lo puede dejar visto para sentencia
articles.standfirst: El GOAT del Trial encara la ronda francesa con el objetivo de seguir con su pleno de victorias. Aún no puede sellar la 20ª corona al aire libre, pero si gana, lo de Países Bajos será un trámite
articles.summary: El GOAT del Trial encara la ronda francesa con el objetivo de seguir con su pleno de victorias. Aún no puede sellar la 20ª corona al aire libre, pero si gana, lo de Países Bajos será un trámite
articles.body: Vuelve la acción en el Mundial de Trial al aire libre. En Cahors (Francia) se reanuda un campeonato que tiene muy bien encarrilado el infalible Toni Bou. El competidor del Repsol Honda HRC acumula un increíble pleno de victorias (Japón, Andorra, Italia y Gran Bretaña) y, como consecuencia de ello, atesora ya 320 puntos en la general del certamen outdoor. Jaime Busto, segundo en la tabla clasificatoria, está situado a 90 puntos del indiscutible líder, mientras que el tercero en discordia, Gabriel Marcelli, cuenta con una desventaja de 91 con respecto a su compañero de escuadra. En la localidad francesa, que acogerá la quinta ronda de la temporada en curso, habrá formato de una única jornada de competición el domingo (es decir, habrá menos puntos en juego). Por esta razón, Bou aún no contará con ningún match-ball para sellar su 40º título mundial de Trial. Eso sí, en Cahors puede dejar totalmente sentenciada esta edición del TrialGP si vuelve arrasar... algo que puede ocurrir con relativa facilidad porque este es un escenario que le va como anillo al dedo al piloto de la Montesa Cota 4RT. En su última visita a esta sede, en 2024, consiguió abrochar el título mundial al aire libre. El caso es que si gana aquí, donde celebrará su 20º entorchado al aire libre será la semana siguiente en la ronda de los Países Bajos. Y el de Piera no oculta que este es un sitio que tiene marcado en rojo en el calendario porque le evoca bonitos recuerdos. “Cahors es una carrera muy especial para mí, ya que hace un par de años logré allí un Mundial, y es un lugar al que siempre llego con muchas ganas. Durante el parón hemos trabajado para descansar y recuperar el físico, y creo que llego en buenas condiciones para afrontar esta recta final. Hemos tenido un inicio de temporada increíble y ahora lo más importante es mantener la concentración, evitar errores y seguir sumando el máximo número de puntos posible. Evidentemente, queremos continuar luchando por las victorias, pero el principal objetivo es asegurar el campeonato”, ha desglosado el GOAT del Trial en unas declaraciones difundidas por su equipo antes de que se celebre la cita gala.

articles.title: Marc Márquez: "Es como en el fútbol, cuando juegan bien, se cansan menos"
articles.standfirst: Compara correr en motos en un circuito favorable con los partidos y los futbolistas
articles.summary: Compara correr en motos en un circuito favorable con los partidos y los futbolistas
articles.body: Marc Márquez no fue primero tras los entrenamientos iniciales y la Práctica de MotoGP del Gran Premio de Aragón, en Motorland. Eso sí, el vigente campeón admitió que optó por no forzar al final. Ve todo apretado y no se confía, aunque reconoce que en este trazado todo le sale más sencillo que en otros. “Llevo la cara de viernes, estoy fresquito, aún. Pero bien. Ha sido un viernes donde hemos salido y me he encontrado cómodo, como esperaba encontrarme en Aragón, pero nunca lo sabes. Me he encontrado bien, pero también se ha visto que, y también lo intuía, que está todo muy apretado. Hemos rodado tres pilotos por debajo del récord y he sido tercero hoy, así que tenemos que seguir trabajando para intentar luchar esa victoria, esa pole e intentar sacar el máximo. No será fácil. No está dicho que estamos en un circuito favorable, o hemos conseguido muchas victorias en el pasado, que vaya a ser fácil. Tendremos que apretar y trabajar mucho durante el fin de semana si queremos sacar el máximo”. “Para mí, cada fin de semana es diferente. Carrera a carrera. Lógicamente, en un circuito donde te salen un poquito más fácil las cosas, esto también te exige menos, te ayuda. A veces es difícil de entender que cuando, como en el fútbol, cuando juegan bien, seguro que se cansan menos. Y cuando estás ahí defendiendo, que juegas mal, que no te salen los pases y esto, te cansas el doble. Pues pasa lo mismo en las motos. En un circuito que te sale fácil, te cansas menos”. “Es innato, porque he trabajado en darle la vuelta a esto, en que fuera en los de derechas y peor en los de izquierdas, lo firmaría porque hay muchos más a derechas en el campeonato. No significa de a derechas no sepa girar; simplemente, que estamos más a la par con los otros y a izquierdas marcamos un poquito la diferencia y me sale un poco más fácil. He intentado trabajar y analizar durante toda mi carrera deportiva el cómo hacer mejor las de derechas, copiar lo de izquierdas, pero es innato, sale natural”. “Esto es como cuando juegas con un equipo más pequeño, pues la victoria es lo normal o cuando juegas con un equipo grande y tú eres el pequeño, si ganas, vives de esa victoria mucho tiempo. Esto también pasa aquí. Cuando estás jugando en uno de los circuitos donde has ganado tanto, como en Sachsenring, si se gana, es lo que tocaba; si no se gana, será la noticia, pero yo soy muy consciente de que cada circuito y cada partido son igual de difíciles y no vale el despiste, sino que estamos en el Mundial y todo el mundo va muy rápido”. “No. Todo el mundo ha apretado igual, para hacer la Q2, para estar en la Q2 directamente, para clasificarse, para preparar la carrera. Hoy se ha visto que estará todo el fin de semana muy apretado y es lo que tiene, cuando hay varios pilotos que se están jugando el Mundial, cuando no te sale uno, te sale otro. Hoy, se han visto un Bezzecchi y un Álex que han ido muy rápido, pero estamos a viernes. Mañana, quizá te sale un Martín y un Di Giannantonio”. “Sí. Ya en Silverstone hizo un gran fin de semana. Han pasado dos semanas más y se ha visto que Bezzecchi se ha caído fuerte esta temporada y no se arruga, no se achanta. Simplemente, es un piloto valiente, rápido y que seguirá yendo rápido toda la temporada”. “Lo teníamos en la estrategia, planeado así, que si en el primer intento salía bien, luego toca minimizar cosas. Entonces, minimizamos riesgos, que es lo importante también en este punto; hay que cogerlos, pero si los puedes minimizar mucho mejor”.

articles.standfirst: Se ve un poco por detrás de Marc y Bezzecchi, pero con buenas sensaciones
articles.summary: Se ve un poco por detrás de Marc y Bezzecchi, pero con buenas sensaciones
articles.body: Álex Márquez ofreció un gran rendimiento en el primer día en el Gran Premio de Aragón de MotoGP, en Motorland, una pista que le gusta. El bicampeón de Cervera batió el récord y estuvo muy cerca de Bezzecchi, el primero, y Marc, el favorito. “No está mal. Creo que hemos hecho un buen trabajo. Es verdad que yo, por la mañana, he empezado bien, venir de Silverstone con un buen resultado te da algo extra y me he sentido bien en un circuito que me gusta y que me sale bastante natural. Es verdad que he sufrido un poquito con el agarre delantero más que el trasero, sobre todo, en frenadas duras como la curva 1, la 8, la 12, la 14. Es ahí donde sufro un pelín más, me falta un pelín de agarre delante, la rueda se bloquea un poquito demasiado y es donde pierdo más, en el sector 3, con lo que es ahí donde hay que concentrarse un pelín más. Hemos dado pasos durante el día importantes y cada vez me he sentido mejor”. “Me sale. Es verdad también que es un circuito difícil, donde cuando das más vueltas, te va un poquito mejor y hemos hecho muchos test aquí, sobre todo cuando estaba en Moto3 y Moto2 y lo conozco muy bien. No hay muchas curvas lentas; lástima el sector 3, que yo lo quitaría, lo haría recto por la recta. Por lo demás, es súper bonito, es muy fluido, llevas la velocidad y ahí es a mí de los circuitos que me gusta”. “Normalmente, los viernes aún están más apretados, hay menos diferencia aún. Marc no ha metido el segundo blando, si no, seguramente, podría ahí haber mejorado un pelín, no sé cuánto, pero bastante. La pole, mañana, será bastante rápida, con menos temperatura. Ha habido un cambio de agarre bastante grande de la mañana a la tarde, con bastantes vueltas de todas las categorías, con más goma en pista. Creo que estamos aún un pasito o medio pasito por detrás de Marc y Bezzecchi, pero cada vez me siento más preparado, un poquito más cerca. Mañana, a ver si conseguimos frenar un poquito más tarde y tener un poquito más de ‘feeling’ (sensaciones) en el tren delantero, que eso creo que nos dará un gran paso de tiempo por vuelta”. “Si te fijas, el año pasado, Bezzecchi sufrió, sobre todo, en la sesión de clasificación, pero, luego, en carrera remontó muchísimo y tenía, más o menos, el mismo ritmo que teníamos las Ducati. Creo que el año pasado, en los circuitos hasta mitad de temporada son un poco engañosos para esto, porque Bezzecchi era nuevo con Aprilia y nunca consiguió hacer buenas sesiones de clasificación o cometía más errores de lo normal. Pero ya, luego, en carrera, cuando se metía en el ritmo, tenía ritmo como nosotros y es ahí donde hay que mirar un poquito mejor. Entonces, ya me esperaba verlo ahí, cerca. Quizá, no tanto, pero que hubiera estado, seguro. Ya lo dije: todos los que se juegan el título, al final, cada fin de semana estarán ahí; nadie va a pinchar muchísimo, de estar de golpe el 12º; todos van a estar muy a la milésima”. “Hacer la pole y ganar la Sprint”. “No. Creo que el Mundial está aún muy apretado, donde queda muchísimo hasta el final, donde hemos visto, sobre todo con las Sprint de por medio, que puede pasar de todo en cualquier momento. Creo que hasta el final esto va a estar abierto y cuando des a alguien ya por descartado, de golpe te saldrá, te hace tres carreras buenas, con 37 puntos. No es como antes, aquí cambia todo en dos fines de semana muchísimo”. "Más que picar el anzuelo, es que él se guarda siempre esa décima, esas dos décimas, no va siempre al límite y es cuando tú tienes el ritmo bien, ahí puedes jugar un poco a eso, pero no de estar guardando durante todo el fin de semana, sino más en ritmo de carrera, él puede jugar un poquito más”.

articles.title: IndyCar dismisses Barranquilla Mayor’s confirmation of 2028 race in Colombia
articles.summary: Mayor Alejandro Char claimed a street race is locked in for April 2028, but the series stresses talks remain in the "earliest stages" with no agreement in pl...
articles.body:
IndyCar has poured cold water on claims made by Barranquilla Mayor Alejandro Char, who publicly announced that the Colombian city had secured an IndyCar event set for April 2028.

Speaking at the launch of the Magdalena River Crossing—as initially reported by prominent Colombian outlet Revista Semana —Mayor Char proclaimed that Barranquilla would host the series along the city's Gran Malecón riverfront. He framed the prospective event as a major milestone for the region and a step toward expanding the series internationally.

"IndyCar is coming to race here," Char stated during the announcement. "It will be racing outside of North America for the first time, and in April 2028, IndyCar will race here, right by the river."

Char emphasized the dramatic urban transformation of the Magdalena riverbank. Once an industrial zone dominated by disconnected warehouses and commercial space, the revitalized waterfront was presented as the centerpiece of a broader strategy to position Barranquilla as a global destination for tourism and premier international sporting events.

However, the sanctioning body quickly pushed back on the Mayor's declarations, clarifying that any reports of a finalized contract are entirely premature.

In a statement provided to Motorsport.com, IndyCar made it clear that while exploratory talks have taken place, formal evaluation of the venue has barely begun:

"We are frequently approached by parties interested in discussing IndyCar racing internationally. We have met with representatives of Barranquilla in Indianapolis but have not yet visited the city ourselves. While the city is interested in hosting an IndyCar race in 2028, we are in the earliest stages of due diligence with this and other prospective opportunities. We are a long way from an agreement and any assumption otherwise is premature."

While Barranquilla leadership remains eager to showcase its rejuvenated riverfront to a global motorsport audience, IndyCar's firm response confirms that a Colombian fixture is far from guaranteed.

articles.title: Pajari toma el mando en un salvaje primer día en Paraguay
articles.standfirst: El caos se apodera del inicio de la 11ª cita del Mundial de Rallyes (WRC) y el finlandés vuelve a tomar el mando tras sus dos victorias seguidas
articles.summary: El caos se apodera del inicio de la 11ª cita del Mundial de Rallyes (WRC) y el finlandés vuelve a tomar el mando tras sus dos victorias seguidas
articles.body: Decían en la ceremonia de salida de la repleta Encarnación, justo antes de iniciar la acción, que el Rally del Paraguay, 11ª cita del 2026 en el Campeonato del Mundo (WRC), podría ostentar, sin problema, el título al mejor rally del mundo. Y tras lo visto en las ocho especiales iniciales de carrera, perfectamente puede levantar la mano para serlo. La locura se apoderó de la prueba sudamericana, con Sami Pajari liderando en un festival de pinchazos, problemas y un posible vuelco a una general del campeonato que lidera Elfyn Evans. Nadie puede irse a dormir tranquilo. "Lo que más miedo da es que ha sido el día más fácil", resumía Hayden Paddon, segundo de la general y uno de los supervivientes a la carnicería. El de Hyundai se quedó a 11,9 de Pajari tras perder el mando en el penúltimo tramo al ver su neumático reventado. Su caso uno de los muchos que sufrieron, pues los problemas iniciaron desde el golpe de Takamoto Katsuta nada más iniciar la acción, pasaron por un pinchazo y rotura de suspensión de un Sébastien Ogier que queda casi descartado de poder defender su corona, otro abandono similar de Thierry Neuville o un parón tras pinchazo de Oliver Solberg, primer líder de la competición. La crisis de los candidatos fue total en la velocidad y los especiales tramos guaranís. Con el punto culminante de la segunda pasada por el larguísimo Yerbateros -de 34 kilómetros- que cambió la general en favor de Pajari y limitó las opciones de un Evans que si bien abre pista, sí puede salir muy beneficiado tras el KO de casi todos los favoritos. Pero el galés pinchó y tras conducir más de 15 kilómetros con una rueda en mal estado sólo puede salvar un tercero. "Y esto sólo es el viernes, toca lo peor", cerraba Pajari. Aunque el finlandés empieza a ver el camino despejado y sus sensaciones son inmejorables. Ya ganó en la velocidad de Estonia, salió beneficiado del brutal accidente de Ogier en Finlandia y es el piloto del momento. Manda en Paraguay con cuidado de las gomas y una velocidad que debe mantener. Aunque más que una prueba de velocidad parece de resistencia. Y es lo que seguirá siendo en la característica grava del corazón de América del Sur. En clave española, la acción quedó marcada por el brutal accidente del asturiano Alejandro Cachón nada más iniciar la acción. El asturiano perdió el control de su Yaris Rally 2 y terminó volcando al golpear con un talud alto en el lateral de la pista. Pierde muchas opciones de título en un WRC2 que comanda el local Diego Domínguez tras el primer día.

articles.title: Lando Norris signs new McLaren contract until end of 2030
articles.summary: In an exclusive BBC Sport interview, Lando Norris explains why he has signed a new contract that will keep him at McLaren until at least the end of 2030.
articles.body:
Lando Norris says signing a new contract that will keep him at McLaren until at least the end of 2030 was "quite an easy yes for me".

The world champion, whose new deal was announced on Saturday, said he "didn't even have a look" at other teams before deciding to commit his future to the team he has been with since his Formula 1 debut in 2019.

"There was some interest from elsewhere," Norris said in an interview with BBC Sport, "but I don't want to go anywhere. I don't want to be with another team. I don't want to spend time with other people.

"That's why it really was probably one of the easiest decisions I've made since being in Formula 1."

The Briton had no need to rush his decision to commit to McLaren because his existing contract still had more than a year to run.

But he says the idea "became a topic of conversation over the last four months or so, but very loosely in the background" and he had no hesitation in agreeing.

Norris says his loyalty to McLaren is based on the relationships he has within the team - starting with chief executive officer Zak Brown and team principal Andrea Stella - and their shared history.

After Norris made his F1 debut in 2019, they spent several years struggling for competitiveness, before their form turned around quickly after Stella was promoted at the end of 2022.

The team won consecutive constructors' championships in 2024 and 2025 - ending a drought that went back to 1998 - and the drivers' title for Norris last year.

The 26-year-old said: "The fact I stuck it through with them and then we went on to obviously have success certainly makes me feel like I don't want to... they didn't give up on me and I didn't give up on them.

"That just creates a very strong bond between everyone that works here. I want to believe that bond stays as strong as it is now 'til I do retire in my career at Formula 1.

"I know that's a long, long way away and I don't want to think of it. But I believe we're in the best place we've ever been even with a tough start to the season. And I believe that we can fight through anything together for sure."

'I don't want to fight through moments with anyone else'

McLaren started this season well off the pace they had shown through 2024 and 2025 as they struggled to get on top of the new rules introduced to F1 this year.

But Norris says that only made him want to stay at the team more.

"That's exactly the situation that doesn't take me away from where I am or doesn't influence anything else," he said.

"I still have had a lot of fun and enjoy working and trying to fight through the tougher moments with the people that I do it with now. I don't want to fight through moments with anyone else.

"This beginning of the year is the perfect example of what doesn't make me turn my head the other way or anything.

"In fact, it's more the opposite. It makes me want to stick with the people that I am with because I believe we can fight back through most circumstances and all circumstances. And I enjoy the fight in some ways just as much as I enjoy the experience of being on top."

He added: "People get too hung up sometimes on saying, 'is it the right place?' I believe it is, but even if it wasn't, the fact that I can just say I'm a driver for McLaren and I race for McLaren, that makes me happy enough."

Title hopes? 'I'm starting the fight to defend it'

McLaren have improved their performance significantly in recent races. After a major upgrade to their car, Norris has won the past two grands prix, in Hungary and the Netherlands.

That has reduced the gap between him and Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli to 83 points with 11 races remaining - although the war in the Middle East may affect the number of races that end up being staged.

Norris said before the British Grand Prix in July that he had been frustrated at not being able to defend his title.

Now, he says: "I'm starting the fight of defending it. I'm trying to. I'm doing my best. We all are. As a team, we're doing our best. They want to allow me to fight for it and of course I just want to fight for it. So, it's a big challenge.

"It's still a big mountain to climb in terms of trying to achieve it. But for a while now, we've been very, very close to being in the position that we are now, where we can fight for wins and podiums and we can fight the people we need to fight against.

"So, I'm certainly more confident than I have been, especially the first part of the year.

"But it still just takes a lot of work and there's a lot of things we need to improve on but we're confident as a team that we can try to achieve it."

Team principal Andrea Stella said: "Lando is an exceptional driver, who combines outstanding natural speed with maturity, consistency and a strong commitment to McLaren but, above all, he is a special human being who is valued by everyone in the team.

"Since joining McLaren as part of our junior programme, he has grown with us and played a central role in bringing the team back to the front of Formula 1.

"This extension gives us important continuity and reinforces our confidence in the direction we are taking together.

"With him and Oscar [Piastri, Norris' team-mate], we know we can count not only on one of the strongest partnerships but also on one of the most united and close-knit teams in Formula 1."

Zak Brown, chief executive officer of McLaren Racing, said: "Lando's journey with the team is a fantastic example of our commitment to identifying, developing and supporting world-class talent, and his achievements speak for themselves."

articles.title: Lando Norris: McLaren driver signs contract extension until 2030 with target of more world championships
articles.summary: Lando Norris commits long-term future to McLaren; reigning world champion agrees multi-year extension to previous deal; the Brit has already driven in a team record 163 grands prix for McLaren; watch the Italian Grand Prix at Monza live on Sky Sports F1 on September 4-6
articles.body:
The 26-year-old Brit's previous extension, which was announced ahead of the start of the 2024 season, was understood to tie him to the team until at least the end of 2027.

He will now stay at McLaren for at least another four seasons with the extended deal to the end of 2030 including "a multi-year option to commit beyond that date".

Norris claimed the 2025 title to become Britain's 11th world champion, and the first McLaren driver to triumph since Lewis Hamilton in 2008.

Saturday's announcement of the new deal follows Norris winning last weekend in the Netherlands to claim the 13th Grand Prix victory of his F1 career.

Norris said: "McLaren is my home, and I'm very pleased to be signing a new contract to keep me with the team until at least 2030.

"When I started this journey nine years ago, I was clear about the goals I wanted to achieve: to get McLaren back to the front and to win championships.

"We've achieved that goal, but we want more, we want to keep on winning, and we know as a team that we're capable of achieving it."

Team principal Andrea Stella described Norris as "an exceptional driver, someone who combines outstanding natural speed with maturity, consistency and a strong commitment to McLaren".

"But above all, he is a special human being who is valued by everyone in the team," added Stella.

"Since joining McLaren as part of our junior programme, he has grown with us and played a central role in bringing the team back to the front of Formula 1."

After McLaren, the reigning constructors' champions, failed to claim a Grand Prix win across the opening 10 rounds of the season, Norris has won back-to-back races to reignite hope that he could yet defend his title.

Norris is fourth in the drivers' standings, 83 points back from leader Kimi Antonelli with 11 rounds remaining. Norris must also leapfrog Antonelli's Mercedes team-mate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, who both trail the Italian by 59 points.

Norris is driving his eighth season for McLaren, having been given his F1 debut by the team as a 19-year-old in 2019. His 163 Grand Prix starts are a team record, with Norris having surpassed fellow Brit David Coulthard's mark of 150 at last year's Qatar Grand Prix.

McLaren's other driver, Oscar Piastri, last year signed a contract extension that ties him to the team until at least the end of the 2028 season.

McLaren were briefly linked with a move for Max Verstappen earlier this summer, but the four-time world champion recently ended speculation over his future by signing a contract extension - also until 2030 - with Red Bull.

On Norris' contract, Stella added: "This extension gives us important continuity and reinforces our confidence in the direction we are taking together.

"With him and Oscar, we know we can count not only on one of the strongest partnerships but also on one of the most united and close-knit teams in Formula 1."

Chief executive Zak Brown said: "[Norris'] journey with the team is a fantastic example of our commitment to identifying, developing and supporting world-class talent, and his achievements speak for themselves.

"Together with Andrea, Oscar and the wider team, Lando has helped drive McLaren into a new papaya era of success... We are extremely excited about what lies ahead and remain fully focused on continuing to compete for wins and championships."

'Four more years fighting for championships'

Norris has played a key role in helping McLaren transition from being a midfield team when he joined to returning to the front of the grid.

He and Piastri led the team to a first constructors' title for 26 years in 2024, before adding his maiden drivers' title the following season after coming out on top of an intense battle with his team-mate and Verstappen.

Asked during an exclusive interview with Sky Sports News whether it was an easy decision to sign an extension, Norris replied: "I would say so.

"After what we've achieved the last two years, over just the fun that we've had together since 2019, nowhere else I want to be, to be honest with you.

"I know we can achieve a lot more together here, exactly where I am, and I'm very excited about our future together."

Norris is open to the idea of spending his whole career at McLaren, and says he would be "so proud" to leave F1 having only driven for the Woking squad.

"I don't know what the future holds," Norris said. "I still, of course, believe that we can win more as a team and win more constructors' and more drivers' championships, and that's why I want to stay here.

"But they are also the only team I've ever been with and the team that I love, and I call this place my home. So, if I do end up just doing my whole career in McLaren, that's something I'll be so proud to say and to carry with me through the rest of my life.

"But I don't know what point I want to go to as a driver. Whether I want to be 30 or 40, 50. I don't know that state yet.

"So, I'm just very, very pleased to, of course, announce I'll be here for four more years and four more years fighting for wins and championships, hopefully."

articles.title: F1 driver contracts: How long are Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Lando Norris and other Formula 1 stars signed for?
articles.summary: Find out how long the likes of Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen and Lando Norris are signed up for at their respective Formula 1 teams; watch every race of the 2026 F1 season, live on Sky Sports and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
Lando Norris agreed a contract extension in August 2026 to stay at McLaren until at least the end of 2030, with options to extend beyond that season.

Norris has been with McLaren since his F1 debut in 2019 and became world champion in 2025.

Oscar Piastri signed a new multi-year contract extension ahead of the 2025 F1 season that will keep him at McLaren until the end of 2028.

Officially, Mercedes announced George Russell only for 2026 after speculation throughout last summer.

But, Sky Sports News understands Russell signed a multi-year contract so will be with Mercedes until at least the end of 2027.

Mercedes confirmed Kimi Antonelli will remain for 2026 at the same time as their October announcement regarding Russell's future.

Sky Sports News understands, like Russell, Antonelli signed a long-term deal that will keep him at Mercedes for at least a third campaign in 2027.

Max Verstappen ended speculation about his future by signing a new Red Bull contract in August 2026 that will see him stay with the team until the end of 2030.

Verstappen citied the possibility of V8 engines returning, confidence in Red Bull and racing in other motorsport categories as some of the reasons behind his new deal.

Isack Hadjar will be the seventh driver in the last eight years to try their hand at being Verstappen's team-mate at Red Bull following his impressive rookie campaign at Racing Bulls.

Hadjar's future will be largely dictated around how close he is to Verstappen, regardless of how strong the RB22 is.

Charles Leclerc penned his latest Ferrari deal in June 2026. As with his previous agreement, announced in January 2024, the team did not publicly comment on the length of his contract, simply saying that it secured Leclerc's future at Maranello "for the coming seasons".

That would take Leclerc up to at least the end of 2028, while there may also be options beyond that to extend further too.

Lewis Hamilton's shock announcement in February 2024 to join Ferrari in 2025 was one of the biggest F1 transfer deals in the sport's history.

Ferrari announced the move as a multi-year deal. Hamilton provided more clarity on the precise length of that term when he confirmed at the 2026 Canadian Grand Prix that he also had a contract in place for at least 2027, which would be his third year at the team. Sky Sports F1 understands Hamilton also holds a unilateral option for 2028 too.

Williams announced during the 2026 summer break a one-year contract extension for Alex Albon that will keep him with the team until the end of 2027.

The short-term nature of the deal perhaps reflects concern in Albon's camp over the team's lack of progress, but also a lack of realistic alternatives being available to him.

A day after Albon's extension was announced, Williams revealed that Sainz had agreed a multi-year extension that appears to tie the Spaniard to the team until at least the end of the 2028 season.

The "multi-year" nature of the deal came as a something of a surprise given Sainz had publicly expressed doubts over remaining with Williams given their poor start to the 2026 season.

Liam Lawson will look to establish himself as the lead driver at Racing Bulls against rookie Arvid Lindblad and should he really impress Red Bull, it should not be ruled out about the possibility of him being in contention to return to the main team.

If that's not possible, Lawson may talk to other teams to secure a spot on the 2027 grid, but he must first deliver some strong results.

British teenager Lindblad is the only rookie on the 2026 grid after impressing Red Bull in his three practice outings last year, finishing sixth in first practice in Mexico City.

The 18-year-old just needs to ensure he does not make any big mistakes and if can match, or beat, team-mate Lawson, at the very least he will have a second season at Racing Bulls.

Fernando Alonso agreed a contract extension in April 2024 to remain with Aston Martin until at least the end of the 2026 F1 season.

Alonso is the oldest driver on the grid and will turn 45 later this year, which would make him the first driver to compete in Formula 1 at that age since Graham Hill in 1975.

Aston Martin appear to be on the backfoot, so there will naturally be questions about whether Alonso will retire at the end of this season.

Lance Stroll is the only driver in the field whose contract details are largely unknown, partly because he is the son of team owner Lawrence Stroll, and appears to have a seat for as long as his father remains in that position.

Stroll has been outperformed by Alonso during their three seasons together but Aston Martin formally announced in June 2024 that the Canadian has a deal for "2025 and beyond".

Oliver Bearman's first full F1 campaign in 2025 saw a mixture of high-profile mistakes and lightning speed - with the latter aspect leading to speculation over whether he could replace Hamilton at Ferrari in the future.

Haas are unlikely to be front-runners in F1 any time soon, so at 20 years old, Bearman could be a key name in the driver market this season, should he impress on the track.

Esteban Ocon's stock has fallen slightly over the last two years after a disappointing end to his time at Alpine in 2024 and being outperformed by Bearman at Haas in 2025.

Ocon will aim to get on top of Bearman in the inter-team battle, which could be important given both drivers have not been confirmed for 2027.

Nico Hulkenberg signed a multi-year contract when he joined Sauber, which is now Audi, in 2025 which means he does not necessarily have a seat beyond this season.

Hulkenberg still seems to enjoy F1 and has not shown any signs of retiring despite being a father and 38 years old.

Gabriel Bortoleto perhaps did not hit the heights many expected after winning the F3 and F2 titles in his rookie seasons on his way to F1.

Bortoleto improved as 2025 went on and is still one of the best young talents on the grid, so it will be in Audi's best interests to keep the 21-year-old.

Pierre Gasly announced a new contract last September to stay at Alpine until at least the end of 2028, having joined the team in 2023.

Gasly has established himself as the lead driver at Alpine and a more competitive car this year could see him cause some surprise results when the top teams trip up.

Franco Colapinto replaced Jack Doohan just six rounds into the 2025 season and recovered from a shaky start to his Alpine career to earn a seat for this season.

The Argentine has impressed Alpine enough to retain his seat for a second full campaign in 2027.

Sergio Perez returns to F1 this year with newcomers Cadillac after a season out of the sport and will be with the American outfit for at least two seasons.

Although Perez was only confirmed for 2026, Sky Sports News understands he signed a multi-year deal.

Valtteri Bottas is also understood to have agreed a multi-year contract that will see him be with Cadillac until at least the end of 2027.

Just like Perez, he spent 2025 on the sidelines but will be hoping to add a few more highlights to his F1 career.
